## Problem

Agent runs on flex can fail when capacity is unavailable because they do not permit standard-tier fallback.

**Why:** Let these runs recover through the gateway's existing fallback policy.

Refs #106462. This change covers the header; timeout validation and run metrics remain separate work.

## Changes

- Flex runs permit standard-tier fallback through `X-PostHog-Flex-Fallback: standard` on OpenAI requests to ai-gateway.
- Default, priority, unset tiers, and the Python and Anthropic paths send no fallback header.

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A{{Agent-server}} -->|Flex tier| G[AI gateway]
    G --> F[Flex attempts only]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    class A phBlue;
    class G,F phRed;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A{{Agent-server}} -->|Flex tier and fallback header| G[AI gateway]
    G --> F[Flex attempts]
    F -->|Eligible failure and fallback enabled| S[Standard attempt]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    class A phBlue;
    class G,F,S phRed;
```

> [!NOTE]
> The gateway must enable fallback. A standard-tier fallback can incur standard-tier charges. No visual changes.

Extended the existing environment test to catch missing flex fallback and accidental fallback on other tiers or gateway paths.

## Problem

A team syncing EasyPost can see what they insured but not what they claimed, and cannot resolve the carrier ids stamped on every shipment and rate they already sync.

- `insurances` records the coverage bought. Nothing records the claim filed against it, so loss, theft and damage outcomes are absent.
- Every shipment and rate carries a `carrier_account_id` and a service code that resolve to nothing in the warehouse.
- Platforms that buy postage on behalf of their users sync shipments referencing an `end_shipper_id` with no table behind it.

These are long-standing gaps from `COVERAGE_GAPS_APPENDIX.md`, not a new EasyPost release.

## Changes

- Four new selectable tables: `claims`, `carrier_accounts`, `carriers`, `end_shippers`.
- `claims` and `end_shippers` sync incrementally on `created_at`, like the nine existing tables.
- `carrier_accounts` and `carriers` sync full refresh only. Neither endpoint exposes a cursor, so offering incremental would let a user pick a sync type that silently re-reads the whole collection every run.
- The endpoint config gains three flags, because the two lookups break assumptions every existing endpoint shared:
  - `paginated` — the lookups answer in one response with no `before_id` and no `has_more`.
  - `supports_start_datetime` — `/end_shippers` paginates by cursor but documents no time filter, so its descending client-side watermark stop is the only bound on an incremental run.
  - `returns_bare_list` — `/carrier_accounts` answers with a bare JSON array instead of the `{"<name>": [...]}` wrapper.
- Canonical column descriptions for the four tables, taken from the EasyPost docs.
- The appendix ticks the four boxes.

Nothing about the nine existing tables changes.

**Endpoints verified, none skipped.** All four exist on v2, the version this source pins:

| Endpoint | Table | Pagination | Time filter | Sync |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [`GET /v2/claims`](https://docs.easypost.com/docs/insurance/claims) | `claims` | `before_id` + `has_more` | `start_datetime` | incremental |
| [`GET /v2/end_shippers`](https://docs.easypost.com/docs/endshippers) | `end_shippers` | `before_id` + `has_more` | none | incremental |
| [`GET /v2/carrier_accounts`](https://docs.easypost.com/docs/carrier-accounts) | `carrier_accounts` | none | none | full refresh |
| [`GET /v2/metadata/carriers`](https://docs.easypost.com/docs/carrier-metadata) | `carriers` | none | none | full refresh |

> [!NOTE]
> EasyPost serves `/v2/carrier_accounts` to production API keys only. A source connected with a test key fails that table.

`carriers` keys on the single-word carrier name, not `id`. The object carries neither an id nor timestamps, so it also declares no partition key.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only. This sandbox has no EasyPost account, so no request ran against the live API. Endpoint shapes come from the vendor docs linked in the table above.

New tests, and the regression each catches:

- Bare-list extraction. `/carrier_accounts` is the only endpoint without the name-keyed wrapper, so extraction that reads the payload shape instead of the endpoint returns nothing for it.
- No pagination on the lookups. A truthy `has_more` in a lookup response, or a stale saved resume cursor, would re-request the same page forever.
- `/end_shippers` omits `start_datetime` on an incremental run and still stops at the watermark.
- Partition settings switch off together when an endpoint has no partition key. A stray mode or format would partition on a column that is not in the row.
- The lookup schemas offer neither incremental nor append.

Two existing tests changed. Both parameterized over every endpoint and asserted `id` primary keys and `created_at` partitioning, which the lookup tables do not have.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

The posthog.com Supported tables section renders from `get_documented_tables()`, so the four tables and their descriptions appear without a docs change.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop (Claude Code), Opus 5

Skills invoked: `/implementing-warehouse-sources`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.

No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "easypost"` and `--search "carrier_accounts"` both returned nothing, and no open PR from the maintainer touches this source.

Each endpoint was checked against docs.easypost.com before implementing. The audit note on `/v2/metadata/carriers` and `/v2/carrier_accounts` did not mention that both are unpaginated lookups, which is where the three new config flags came from. The audit note described `/v2/claims` as absent; that is correct, `insurances` covers only the policy.

Public artifact: the diff and this description draw on the vendor's public API docs and the repo's own appendix. Nothing carries session material.

body:
## Problem

- A CDC table reset from the app or the API can lose its rows when a sync of the table is still finishing.
- The resync button, a table-mode switch, re-enabling a table's sync, and Repair CDC all reset right after asking the running sync to stop, or with no stop request at all.
- A cancel only asks the workflow to stop. The loader still applies batches the sync queued, and the final one hands over, flipping the table to streaming with `reset_pipeline` still set.
- The next streaming run then wipes the table and replays only the change buffer.
- #106270 fixes the same race for TRUNCATE and slot recovery inside capture. This layer covers the request paths, which cannot wait for a later capture run by themselves.

## Changes

- When a sync of the table could still hand over, these paths pause the table's schedule and set `cdc_reset_pending` with `trigger`, instead of resetting.
  Capture then finishes the reset once the sync stops (#106270), unpauses the schedule, and starts the new snapshot.
- With no sync in the way, they reset at once, as before.
- A failed stop check also hands the reset to capture, because capture retries it.
- Re-enabling a table leaves its schedule paused while its reset is pending, so no sync runs on the old state first.
- Capture merges its own reset into the pending key under the row lock, so a request's `trigger` survives a TRUNCATE in the same run.
- After handing a reset over, the request starts a capture run right away, and recreates the capture schedule if it is gone (`trigger_cdc_extraction_schedule`).
  Otherwise the last capture run could have looked for resets just before the key was written, and a missing schedule would never finish the reset. A source marked broken, or with capture paused after a non-retryable error, is left to Repair CDC or resume, which restart capture themselves.
- Every write that stages a reset bumps a `generation` on the key, and capture drops only the reset it finished.
  Field equality could not tell an identical reset, staged while the snapshot was starting, from the finished one, and the table would keep a paused schedule with no reset left to unpause it.
- The admin resync and `resync_schemas_non_billable` refuse instead, with "A sync of this table is still stopping. Retry in a minute."
  They start their own non-billable run, which capture cannot start for them.
- `hand_reset_to_capture_if_sync_running` in `cdc/snapshot_lane.py` holds the shared check. The API reaches it through the lazy `source_management` facade.
- Not changed: `migrate_cdc_source_to_buffered --rollback` still resets right after a cancel. #105912 deletes that command.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_a_reset_is_left_to_capture_while_the_tables_sync_can_still_hand_over` covers the resync, table-mode switch, and re-enable requests with a sync still stopping. It checks for a pending reset, a paused schedule, no reset, and no trigger.
- `test_repair_cdc_cancels_running_cdc_jobs` now also checks that Repair CDC leaves the busy table to capture and does not resume or trigger its schedule.
- `test_a_pending_reset_finishes_before_the_read_once_the_sync_stopped` gains a case where capture starts the snapshot for a reset a request handed over.
- `test_a_cdc_reset_is_refused_while_the_tables_sync_can_still_hand_over` covers the admin resync refusal.
- `test_a_reset_staged_while_the_snapshot_was_starting_is_left_pending` also stages an identical reset through the real request-side merge. That case fails without the generation.
- `test_triggering_capture_recreates_a_schedule_that_is_gone` and the hand-over test cover the capture trigger.
- Each new case fails with its fix removed.
- Not run: an end-to-end check against a real Temporal cancel and loader.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

- Stacked on #106270, which adds the capture side of `cdc_reset_pending`.
- Skills: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/stacking-prs`.
- CodeRabbit CLI: three findings.
  - Fixed: re-enable unpaused the schedule while the reset was pending.
  - Fixed: capture rebuilt the pending key from a stale in-memory config.
  - Rejected: fail the hand-over when the schedule pause fails. No reset is staged until capture pauses the schedule itself and raises if it cannot. A sync that starts meanwhile cannot hand over into a staged reset. Raising would also fail a table-mode switch after the new mode is saved, leaving the new table unseeded.
- Bot review follow-ups: CodeRabbit's outside-diff "guarantee a capture run" finding and its identical-reset race are both fixed in fc17350 (capture trigger, reset generation); CodeRabbit CLI on that commit: no findings.

## Problem

- An agent preparing a PR for the merge queue reports it green while GitHub and Trunk still block it.
- A push can start two runs of a workflow for one head, and the concurrency group cancels one. The cancelled run's checks stay on the head.
- GitHub's merge box counts them, `statusCheckRollup` reads `FAILURE`, and Trunk holds the PR at "Not ready". A newer green check with the same name does not clear them.
- The Depot check-run reference says to read the newest check per name. That rule gives the verdict, but agents also applied it to merge readiness.

## Changes

- `/merging-prs` preflight: cancelled runs on the head are checked before the failing-checks stop. It lists them on GitHub and Depot and reruns them, with the developer's permission.
- The GitHub rerun goes through the API, because `gh run rerun` returns 404 for the org-level `semgrep` workflow.
- The Depot check-run reference: the newest check per name gives the verdict, not merge readiness.
- Skill text only. No workflow or code changes.

## How did you test this code?

- Seen on [fetch depot ci job logs](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106114): 22 cancelled duplicate runs held Trunk at "Not ready" while the newest run of every required check was green. Rerunning them cleared it.
- The `jq` filter in the new recipe ran against that PR's head.
- `hogli lint:skills` passes.

## Problem

- PostHog Code cloud runs on GLM-5.2 fail about 15 seconds in, before the first turn.
- The free-tier onboarding session runs on GLM-5.2 (`ONBOARDING_SESSION_FREE_MODEL`), so a new free-tier user's first cloud run fails.
- At session start, `claude-agent-sdk` checks the model with a `max_tokens: 1` request.
- Baseten rejects it with `400 max_tokens must be at least 2 for this deployment`. GLM-5.3 on Baseten returns the same error.
- The failures started after #104347 moved sandboxes to `claude-agent-sdk` 0.3.270 ([alert](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0BSZN0A61L/p1790334578452149)).

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  sdk{{"claude-agent-sdk model check"}} -->|"max_tokens 1"| gw["llm-gateway"]
  gw -->|"max_tokens 1"| bt["Baseten"]
  bt -->|"400"| fail["Run fails"]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  class sdk phBlue;
  class gw,bt phRed;
  class fail phYellow;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  sdk{{"claude-agent-sdk model check"}} -->|"max_tokens 1"| gw["llm-gateway raises it to 2"]
  gw -->|"max_tokens 2"| bt["Baseten"]
  bt -->|"200"| ok["Session starts"]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  class sdk phBlue;
  class gw,bt phRed;
  class ok phYellow;
```

## Changes

- Claude-adapter sessions on Baseten models start again.
- `_inject_baseten_params` raises `max_tokens`, `max_completion_tokens` and `max_output_tokens` to 2 when they are below 2.
- That helper runs on all three Baseten paths: Anthropic Messages, Chat Completions and Responses.
- Limits of 2 or more pass through unchanged.

```diff
 make_baseten_{anthropic,completion,responses}_call
   _inject_baseten_params
     map the model to its Baseten id
     force streaming usage
+    raise token limits below 2 to 2
   litellm → Baseten
```

body:
## Problem

- A change to a detector in the image-scrub sidecar has two effects: the CPU cost per image, and the subjects that stay readable in the stored image.
- No tool measured both effects together.
- `npm run eval` reads the stored image with OCR. For a 1080p capture that image is about 161×90, so most detector misses do not show in the eval.
- On Apple silicon, ONNX Runtime runs fp32 convolutions on the SME matrix unit. Graviton has no SME, so Mac timings overstate fp32 speed.

## Changes

- `dev/text-det-bench.ts` runs text detectors through the production pre-processing, post-processing, fill margins and scale plan.
- It reports the single-thread cost and the coverage of each labelled word. It checks its baseline against `src/dbnet.ts` box for box.
- `dev/face-bench.ts` compares YuNet sizes, int8 builds and input sizes on a WIDER FACE val subset and on composites with faces at swept sizes.
- `dev/code-bench.ts` measures the cost of zxing against its input scale. It checks which generated codes stay decodable from the stored image.
- `dev/text-det-setup.ts` and `face-bench.ts --setup` download pinned, checksummed models and labelled public images.
- `dev/text-det-corpus.ts` renders synthetic images with an exact box for each word.
- `dev/text-det-quantize.py` builds static int8 models. `dev/text-det-dynamic-hw.py` lets the docTR exports accept any input size.
- `--no-kleidiai` and `--latency` switch off the KleidiAI kernels, so Mac timings stay closer to Graviton.
- All files are under `dev/`, so production behavior does not change.
- The benches found these candidates on a c6g.4xlarge (Graviton2). The costs are weighted to the production image-size mix.

| Stage | Candidate | Stage cost | Readable subjects left visible |
|---|---|---|---|
| Text | PP-OCRv6 tiny int8, canvas sized from the stored image | −53% | 22 of 7,155 words (27 today) |
| Faces | YuNet-n int8 at the native input size | −63% | 14 of 220 faces (16 today) |
| Codes | zxing at 3.96 times the stored scale | −37% | 0 of 119 codes (0 today) |

- Separate PRs will carry the production changes.

## How did you test this code?

- Each bench ran end to end on an M4 Pro and on a c6g.4xlarge (Graviton2).
- The text baseline matched `detectTextDbnet` on all 248 images, on both machines.
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint` pass in the sidecar.
- No new tests, because the change adds dev scripts only.
- The diff has no event code, so the `test-new-events-schema` label does not apply.

body:
## Problem

An on-call engineer handling a poison message cannot act on the crash log alone. The `Step <name> threw` line the Node ingestion framework logs before the process exits carries only the topic, partition and offset of the message. To park the message with an event restriction they need its `token` and event `uuid`, so the runbooks send them to Kafbat to seek the offset first ([charts#16335](https://github.com/PostHog/charts/pull/16335)).

## Changes

- `KafkaDebugContext` gains `headers`. The `Step <name> threw` log line, and the fan-out crash lines that log the same context, now show the message's `token`, `event` and `uuid`. Those are the three headers a restriction needs. `distinct_id` can be an email address and `session_id` is customer-controlled, so an allowlist keeps them and any other header out of the log.
- The context is built for every message and read only on the crash path, so the headers are rendered by a getter on read. Nothing changes on the happy path.
- Chunk-step crashes keep the offsets-only aggregate; a chunk fails as a whole, so per-message headers there would not point at the culprit.
- Mechanical: `createKafkaDebugContext` destructures the message instead of reading fields one by one.

## How did you test this code?

- `jest src/ingestion/framework/step-pipeline.test.ts src/ingestion/framework/base-chunk-pipeline.test.ts`: the crash test builds the message with `token`, `uuid`, `event`, `distinct_id` and `session_id` headers and asserts the first three appear in the logged context and the last two do not; a second test asserts a message with no headers logs `headers: undefined`. Before this change the first assertion fails because the context has no `headers` key.
- `eslint` and `prettier --check` on the two files.
- `tsc --noEmit` reports no errors in `src/ingestion/framework`; the image build's `tsc` caught a fixture typing error in the test, fixed by typing the header array as `MessageHeader[]`.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

No public docs change. The crash runbooks in PostHog/charts are updated to read the ids from the log line in [charts#16353](https://github.com/PostHog/charts/pull/16353); no `skip-inkeep-docs` label needed.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.1

- Local Claude Code session, no shareable link. Tools used: gh, git, jest, eslint, prettier, tsc. No repo skills were invoked.
- Duplicate search: `gh pr list --state open --search "crash log headers debug context"` found no other PR on this.
- Patch coverage: every changed line in `helpers.ts` runs under the two step-pipeline tests.
- New events schema: not touched.
- Public artifact: nothing in this PR comes from a customer conversation, ticket or log; the fixture values are invented.
- CodeRabbit CLI: local pass skipped, the CLI was not run in this session.
- Decisions: a null-header guard was added after a review comment and then reverted, because node-rdkafka's binding encodes every consumed header value as a Buffer, so the `MessageHeader` type is accurate. An allowlist of `token`, `event` and `uuid` replaced dumping all headers after two security findings about `distinct_id` and `session_id`.

## Problem

Opening a nested project folder from the terminal can leave the Files sidebar showing an expanded, empty parent.
Expanded folders skip missing data, and a late root response can close an already-open Unfiled branch.

## Changes

- Load missing ancestor data and the requested folder even when their tree nodes are already expanded.
- Keep Unfiled open when the root finishes loading.
- Preserve cached pages when reopening folders; fetch further pages only through Load more.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Empty expanded folder](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/46c027fd18a1869988d277a3725854299d3c416b/2026/09/95f11ae8-1f60-420c-8dae-cd3d13d0e1a8.png) | ![Nested folder and contents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/772bc6a5ac71e0cf22c90997bcf48ca29214fc41/2026/09/2479acad-06bc-4857-9503-8b6c4b3ec5c4.png) |

<details>

body:
## Problem

- People building error tracking alerts on destinations cannot show who an issue is assigned to, because the payload holds only a user or role id.
- Issue lifecycle events carry `assignee` as a JSON string, for example `{"type":"user","id":1234}`. The key is missing when the issue is unassigned.
- Hog templates cannot resolve that id to a person, so a message can say "assigned" or "unassigned" and nothing more.
- The alert authoring skill reference does not mention the assignee, so PostHog AI guesses at its shape.

## Changes

- Issue lifecycle events for destinations now carry `assignee_name` and `assignee_email` when the issue has an assignee. A template can use `{event.properties.assignee_name ?? (event.properties.assignee ? 'Assigned' : 'Unassigned')}`.
- The name is the user's full name, or their email when they have no name. A role gets its role name and no email.
- A user who has left the organization keeps their assignments, so the events keep `assignee` but leave out their name and email.
- One lookup in the new `logic/assignees.py` feeds both event producers. It joins the user, role and membership onto the assignment query that manual transitions already ran, so they make no extra query.
- Created, reopened and spiking events make one extra query in their Temporal activity.
- The Temporal path adds the names only while the current assignment still matches the `assignee` that cymbal snapshotted at ingestion. Otherwise a reassignment in between gives a name that contradicts `assignee`.
- The alert authoring skill reference documents the three assignee properties and the unassigned fallback.
- Mechanical: `assignee_property` moves to `logic/assignees.py`, so the Temporal activities can import it without an import cycle through the Temporal package.

> [!NOTE]
> Native alerts (behind the native alerts flag) are untouched. Nothing under `temporal/alerts/` changes, and the native alert inputs do not carry the new fields.

> [!NOTE]
> `assignee_email` sends a teammate's email to customer-configured destinations. The actor's email already goes out in `person.properties.email`. Drop the field if reviewers prefer the name alone.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_side_effects.py`: a new parametrized test covers the snapshot guard on the internal event for the same assignee, a reassignment and an unassignment since ingestion. The oversized-event test pins both fields in the full property set.
- `test_error_tracking_api.py`: the assign test checks the assignee properties for a named user, a user with no name (email fallback) and a role.
- `test_error_tracking_api.py`: a status change on an issue assigned to a removed member keeps `assignee` and leaves out the name and email. This test fails without the membership check.
- The fallback template ran in the Python Hog VM for an unassigned issue, an assignee with no name, and a named assignee.
- Not checked: the Node CDP consumer and a real destination delivery. The properties reach destinations through the existing internal event path.

## Problem

- A new Salesforce source can fail every sync with `404 Client Error: Not Found` on the `/services/data/v68.0/query` path.
- [#101532](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/101532) made v68.0 (Winter '27) the default on 2026-09-16, so each new source is pinned to it.
- Salesforce moves orgs onto a new release in waves over several weeks. An org still on Summer '26 does not serve any v68.0 path.
- The 404 is not in the non-retryable map, so the sync retries each run and stores the raw URL, which includes the org's instance host.

## Changes

- New Salesforce sources are created on v67.0 again, which every org serves.
- `supported_versions` drops v68.0, and `default_version` goes back to v67.0. The version invariant test requires the default to be the newest declared version.
- Rows already pinned to v68.0 keep their pin and request path, because a pin is honored even when it is no longer declared. They recover when Salesforce upgrades their org. The alternative, a repin migration, would move working pins in orgs that already run Winter '27.
- A code comment records the rule: declare a Salesforce release's version only after it reaches every production org.
- The 404 stays retryable. Marking it non-retryable would switch off a sync that recovers by itself when the org upgrades.

## How did you test this code?

- Updated the version tests in `test_salesforce_source.py` and `test_salesforce.py` for the v67.0 default. The dispatch test still covers a retired v68.0 pin building its own path.
- Ran the Salesforce tests and `sources/tests/test_source_versions.py`.

## Problem

- A Postgres sync to a Neon database that refuses PostHog's IP keeps failing every run, and the error panel shows raw driver text with hosts and IPs.
- Neon uses two wordings: "This IP address ... is not allowed to connect to this endpoint", and "... access this endpoint from a blocked network" when the project blocks public access.
- Neither wording matches the existing Supavisor key (`address not in tenant allow_list`), so the batch path retries the failure and stores the raw message.
- On the CDC path the same rejection falls into the retryable `CONNECTION_FAILED` bucket and retries without end.
- This failure class did not reach error tracking, because retried failures do not create exceptions.

## Changes

- The customer now sees what went wrong and what to change, and the sync stops instead of retrying:
  - IP allow list: "Your database provider rejected the connection because PostHog's IP address isn't on its IP allow list. Add PostHog's egress IP addresses to that allow list, then re-enable the sync."
  - Blocked network: "Your database provider blocks connections from the public internet, so PostHog can't connect. Allow public access for PostHog's IP addresses, then re-enable the sync."
- `PostgresSource.get_non_retryable_errors` gets one key for each Neon wording.
- `classify_postgres_cdc_error` maps both wordings to `HOST_UNREACHABLE`, which already tells the customer to allow PostHog's IP addresses.
- Only these two wordings change. The insertion point in the CDC classifier stays clear of the hunk in [#105642](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/105642).

## How did you test this code?

- Added a parameterized test in `test_postgres.py` for both Neon wordings. It fails if either key is removed or is shadowed by a key with a different message.
- Added two cases to `TestClassifyPostgresCDCError`. They fail if either wording falls back to the retryable bucket.

## Problem

Numeric evaluation reports can describe a threshold change as a performance regression, even when the displayed comparison shows no change.
The agent sees historical snapshot rates without their passing rules alongside metrics recalculated under the current rule.
Hog reports also lack the source needed to interpret units and can mistake optional reasoning for missing instrumentation.

## Changes

- Include saved passing rules and their match status in the numeric report history index.
- Direct comparisons to current-rule period metrics, keeping threshold changes separate from performance changes.
- Supply Hog source as evaluation criteria and explain that reasoning is optional.
- Qualify comparisons when scoring consistency is unknown and report insufficient data when either pass rate is missing.
- Encode Hog source as untrusted JSON with escaped backticks. This does not guarantee prompt-injection protection.

Existing reports retain their snapshots. No UI layout changes.

Regression tests cover matching, different, and missing historical rules; Hog source propagation; and the comparison instructions.
Ran the report tool, graph, and activity suites locally. Live LLM report generation has not been checked with this patch.

## Problem

Part of #104853.

- The stable chunk build (#105531) reaches a browser only when someone opts in by hand with `?stable_chunks=1`.
- That cannot run an A/B test. The goal is a 50% split of logged-in users, compared on LCP.

## Changes

- Logged-in users get the stable build when the `stable-chunk-names` flag is on for them.
- `stable_chunks_choice(request, feature_flags)` in `posthog/stable_chunks.py` decides, with early returns in this order:
  1. `?stable_chunks=` param: `1` serves stable, any other value serves the current build.
  2. `ph_stable_chunks` cookie: `1` or `0`.
  3. The `stable-chunk-names` flag, for an authenticated user only.
  4. Otherwise the current build.
- The flag value comes from the bootstrap's `get_all_flags(..., only_evaluate_locally=True)` result, which the template context already computed.
  - No second evaluation, no network call, and no server `$feature_flag_called` event.
  - posthog-js gets the same value, so `$feature/stable-chunk-names` on events matches the build served.
  - A missing local definition or a failed evaluation leaves the flag out of the result, which means the current build.
- `?stable_chunks=0` now stores a 30-day `0` cookie instead of deleting the cookie. An explicit opt-out then beats the flag.
- A failed stable entry now reloads with `?stable_chunks=fallback`, not `=0`.
  - That one response serves the current build and writes no cookie.
  - The next navigation tries the stable build again, so a transient failure does not opt a flagged user out for 30 days.
  - The fallback response never serves stable, whatever the cookie or flag says, so the reload cannot loop.
  - The existing `replaceState` already strips any `stable_chunks` value from the address bar.

> [!NOTE]
> **Rollout.** Create the boolean flag `stable-chunk-names` in project 2 at 0%, then ramp it. Measure LCP on `$web_vitals`, broken down by `$feature/stable-chunk-names`. Setting the flag to 0% is the kill switch.
> #106504 (immutable CSS names) already merged, so the test does not understate the stable build's CSS caching.

## How did you test this code?

- `posthog/test/test_stable_chunks.py`, run locally against a temporary Postgres with ClickHouse stubbed:
  - A precedence table on `stable_chunks_choice`: param beats cookie and flag, cookie beats flag, flag on or off, missing definition, anonymous user, and `fallback` beating a cookie or flag of `1`. Catches a reordering of the precedence.
  - Cookie persistence: `0` stores a 30-day opt-out, `fallback` stores nothing. Catches the fallback reload opting a user out.
  - Through `get_context_for_template` with `posthoganalytics.get_all_flags` mocked: the flag picks the build, the bootstrap carries the same flags, and evaluation stays local. Catches the build and the bootstrap disagreeing. A mutation that stops passing the bootstrap flags fails this test.
- `common/esbuilder` Jest suites pass. No test covers the `copyIndexHtml` boot script, so a local frontend build was inspected instead: the `{% if stable_chunks %}` branch of `frontend/dist/index.html` sets `stable_chunks` to `fallback`, and both branches strip the param.
- Not checked: a real browser with the flag on, since the flag does not exist yet.

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

None.

body:
## Problem - The session replay image-fetch lane falls behind its frontier topic, and Kafka retention deletes records before the lane reads them. - Each pod joins one batch from every group member into one fetch pass. The pass resolves only when its slowest URL finishes, so one slow URL holds back every partition on the pod. - The join exists for origin diversity ([PostHog/posthog#89982](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/89982)): one partition's batch has few origins, so per-origin limits leave request slots idle. - Overlapped passes also count registrable-domain slots per pass. Two passes from the same partitions both claim a domain's slots, and the request scheduler refuses the excess as `connection_limit`. ## Changes - New mode behind `SESSION_RECORDING_ML_IMAGE_FETCH_CONTINUOUS_POOL` (default `false`, so nothing changes until a deploy sets it). - Each group member batch adds its URLs to one candidate pool for the pod and finishes when its own URLs finish. A slow URL now delays only its own batch's offset commit. - The pool counts registrable-domain and origin slots across the pod, so batches share a domain's limit instead of each claiming it. - Workers take the eligible domain whose oldest URL is the oldest. Age order prevents starvation, and domains with long queues still get their full limit. - An origin in its crawl delay is not eligible until the delay passes, so no request slot waits on a crawl delay. - At a batch's pass deadline, its queued URLs leave the pool as `pass_deadline`, the same outcome as today. - A member reads its next batch when fewer than `..._POOL_REFILL_RUNNABLE_URLS` (default 100) of its queued URLs can run. A domain counts only up to its limit, so a window full of one hot domain still refills. `..._POOL_MAX_QUEUED_URLS_PER_MEMBER` (default 2,000) bounds memory and crash replay. - A fetch worker that finds nothing eligible gives room to every member under that limit. Queued URLs can count as runnable but still wait on a crawl delay or on another member's hold on a domain. - The room wait caps at 30 s, below consumer-v2's 60 s stalled-loop check. After the cap a member reads its next batch anyway, so its queue can pass the limit by about one batch until pass deadlines remove URLs. - Crawl-history reads, writes and republish flushes stay per batch. The store already sends fixed-size calls, so this adds only partly filled calls. ### Before ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff; classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000; classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000; M1[Member 1 batch] --> J[Joiner] M8[Member 8 batch] --> J J --> P[One fetch pass] P --> D[All batches resolve
after the slowest URL] class M1,M8 phYellow; class J,P phBlue; class D phGray; ``` ### After ```mermaid flowchart LR classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff; classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000; classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000; M1[Member 1 batch] --> Q[Pod candidate pool] M8[Member 8 batch] --> Q Q --> W[Fetch workers] W --> B1[Batch 1 resolves] W --> B8[Batch 8 resolves] class M1,M8 phYellow; class Q,W phBlue; class B1,B8 phGray; ``` Mechanical: the `IndexedPriorityQueue` export, two read-only `HostBudget` queries, the runner's shared pass tail, and the README and implementation notes. ## How did you test this code? - New `fetch-candidate-pool.test.ts` covers age order across batches, release of domain slots, crawl-delay holds, deadline expiry, withdrawal after a failure, and the refill window. It catches a pool that serves newer URLs first, lets a held origin block others, or counts a hot domain past its limit. - `fetch-runner.test.ts` runs four existing behavior tests in both modes: publish, fatal error, lost publish, and pass deadline. A new pool case checks that two batches share one domain's limit. - A pool test checks that an idle worker gives a member room while its runnable URLs wait on crawl delays. It fails with the signal removed. - `pool-window-batch-handler.test.ts` checks that a member returns once its batch is admitted with room, and returns at the 30 s cap while the window stays full. - The server wiring test checks the lookahead in pool mode, and that each member routes through its own pool window instead of the joiner. - Mutation checks: removing the pod-wide domain cap fails the new runner case, and reversing the age order fails three pool tests. - Not run: `dynamodb-crawl-history.integration.test.ts`, which needs a local DynamoDB. No production run yet. The flag stays off until a charts change enables it. - Event-table coverage: no event ingestion or event reads change, so this PR has no `test-new-events-schema` label. ## Release status - [x] No feature flag controls this change - [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users - [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone ## Automatic notifications - [ ] Publish to changelog? ## Docs update The lane's README (requirement 5.21) and implementation notes describe the new mode. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted) **Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 - Robbie directed the design during an investigation of the lane's throughput. The design doc was reviewed before implementation. - Design choices from that review: selection never looks at the partition, so slots are never idle while eligible work exists. The per-partition window applies only to admission and counts runnable URLs. - Cross-partition micro-batching of DynamoDB calls was left out of v1 as not worth its complexity. It is the next step if throttling shows up. - Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`. - CodeRabbit: not run, at the user's standing instruction. - Duplicate search: `gh pr list --search "image fetch pool"` found no open PR. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

body:
## Problem

- People who search the filter picker in the wrong tab get empty or poor results. The most common case is `email` in the events or event properties tab, and `url` in the person properties tab.
- `email` and `url` are the two most common searches. Picker telemetry shows `email` almost always ends as a person property and `url` as an event property.
- PostHog hosts a decision model, JevK5, that classifies short text fast. This PR tests whether it helps here, as an A/B test, before anyone builds more on it.

## Changes

- **Banner arm:** when the model is confident the search belongs in another tab, the picker shows "Looking for person properties?" with a button that switches the tab.
- **Promote arm:** in the "All" list, the predicted group moves to the top. This happens only while the results still show skeletons, so no row moves under the cursor.
- **Control arm:** the picker does not change. It still asks the model and captures the answer, so the analysis can compare the same searches across arms.
- A new core endpoint, `taxonomic_search_intent/classify`, asks one multiple choice question over the tabs the picker shows. It caches answers per team for a day, uses a 2 s timeout, and has its own throttle, so picker use never takes from the PostHog AI budget.
- The code lives in core (`posthog/taxonomic_search_intent/`, `posthog/api/taxonomic_search_intent.py`) because the picker is a shared core component. It does not depend on `products/ml_inference`.
- The endpoint reaches the model through `build_system_one_client` in `posthog/llm`, the shared System One client from #106735. It has no TypeSafe fallback, because a search is customer text. Without a gateway the endpoint answers 503, and the picker stays as it is.
- The question, the tab meanings and the confidence threshold come from the managed prompt `taxonomic-filter-search-intent` in the PostHog project, at its `production` label. A new wording ships by moving the label, with no deploy.
- A background thread refreshes that prompt once a minute, so a request never waits on the fetch. A bundled copy in `search_intent_prompt.py` is the fallback when there is no key, the fetch fails, or a config part is malformed.
- Value-shaped input never goes to the model. An email address, a URL, a path, a long digit run or an opaque token such as a session id is matched by pattern, or skipped. A path matches with any query or fragment, and a token matches in any word of the search.
- The cache holds each answer as JSON text and validates it on read, because the Django cache pickles what it stores.
- A one-shot eval suite (`hogli evals eval_search_intent`) scores tab match, switch recall and switch precision over 30 invented cases. Precision is the number to protect, because a wrong suggestion is worse than none.
- New events: `taxonomic filter search intent predicted` (every arm) and `taxonomic filter search intent switched` (banner accept). The predicted event carries `promptVersion`, so results split by prompt version.
- Mechanical: regenerated OpenAPI types, a Storybook story, and inline kea types.

> [!NOTE]
> One flag gates the change: `taxonomic-filter-search-intent`. It assigns the experiment arms in the picker, and the endpoint checks it for the requesting person, so a person outside the flag gets a 404. It stays PostHog-only for now, for manual testing in production before any experiment.

### Banner arm in the app

A person searches `email` in the "Event properties" tab, gets the suggestion, and switches to "Person properties".

![search-intent-banner](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/dfa68e66734561d9983d4133d424cccdb76ffc2c/2026/09/429f48dd-a425-4ede-830d-c7c681dd919e.gif)

### Every arm in Storybook

`Filters/Taxonomic Filter`, stories `SearchIntent*`:

| Control: "All" list keeps its order | Promote: person properties move to the top |
| --- | --- |
| ![story-control-keeps-order](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/dfa68e66734561d9983d4133d424cccdb76ffc2c/2026/09/dbee94b3-baf2-468e-b05b-72c0ef192ce0.png) | ![story-promotes-group](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/dfa68e66734561d9983d4133d424cccdb76ffc2c/2026/09/076b42cf-3ae8-44b0-854a-9d7940ba697e.png) |

| Banner, 900px | Banner, narrow scene |
| --- | --- |
| ![search-intent-wide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/e2e051dcfef02e09fb209ee54a44665aeee4e91c/2026/09/4bfc9bdf-9da5-4417-bae4-1dcf6a95fa6a.png) | ![story-suggests-another-tab-narrow](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/dfa68e66734561d9983d4133d424cccdb76ffc2c/2026/09/5b461861-634c-443d-a371-033908d0f625.png) |

## How did you test this code?

- `test_classify.py` and `test_taxonomic_search_intent.py` catch a value (email, URL, digits) that reaches the model, an answer outside the offered tabs, a switch suggestion from the "All" tab or from a weak answer, a cache miss on a repeated search, and endpoint failures that are not a plain 404 or 503.
- They also catch a path with a query string or a token inside a multiword search that reaches the model, a prompt config with more options than the gateway takes, and a missing gateway that returns a 500.
- They also catch a malformed prompt config that breaks the picker, a new prompt version or another team that reuses cached answers, and a request that waits on the prompt fetch.
- `taxonomicSearchIntentLogic.test.ts` catches a request for a person outside the experiment, a banner that outlives its search, a control arm that changes the picker, a promotion after reveal, and repeated requests after a 404.
- Ran in the cloud sandbox after the move to core: both backend test files, `mypy` on the moved code, `lint:tach`, `product:lint --all`, the module-collision and database-free test invariants, `build:openapi`, the `taxonomicSearchIntentLogic` Jest test and `typescript:check`.
- Not run: `semgrep` security rules, because semgrep crashes in the sandbox. CI runs them.
- Ran locally before the move: the full `TaxonomicFilter/` Jest folder and the Storybook stories below.
- Rendered the four `SearchIntent*` stories in Storybook (screenshots above).
- Recorded the banner flow in the local dev stack with Playwright. The stack has no AI gateway, so the recording answers the classify call in the browser with the model answer for `email`. Everything else in the flow is the real app. The promote arm is not in the video, because the local project pins the email property at the top anyway.
- Recorded the three arms with Playwright against temporary Storybook stories. Those stories are not in the diff.
- Not run: the eval suite against the model, because this sandbox has no AI gateway credentials. No CI job runs harness evals, so the suite runs by hand. It stops with an error when the gateway is not configured.
- `confident_threshold` (0.6) in the prompt config is a starting value. Tune it from the first eval run. Set `SEARCH_INTENT_PROMPT_VERSION` to score a draft version before the label moves.
- Not checked: whether the production `POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY` can read prompts. If it cannot, every answer uses the bundled copy and `promptVersion` is null.
- Not run locally: the endpoint tests, because this laptop has no ClickHouse. CI runs them.
- Not labeled `test-new-events-schema`: the diff reads no event tables.

## Problem

- A freshly started heatmaps, clientwarnings, errortracking or ai pod resolves teams one token at a time on its first batches.
- After a rollout reassigns partitions to new pods, those pods process slowly until their team cache warms, so consumer lag rises for a few minutes.
- The analytics pipeline avoids this with `prefetchTeamsStep`, a chunk step that loads all of a chunk's tokens in one batched call.
- The other pipelines that call `.resolveTeam()` never got that step.
- The ai and errortracking pipelines also run hog transformations, and they load each team's transformation functions one team at a time too.

## Changes

- The heatmaps, clientwarnings, errortracking and ai pipelines now run `prefetchTeamsStep` before `.parseMessage()`, as analytics does.
- The step reads the existing `TEAMS_PREFETCH_ENABLED` flag, which defaults to `false`, so nothing changes until a deployment turns it on.
- Reusing the flag keeps rollback a config-only change per lane, rather than a code revert.
- The ai and errortracking pipelines also run `prefetchHogFunctionsStep`, gated by the existing `HOG_FUNCTIONS_PREFETCH_ENABLED` flag (default `false`).
- Hog-function prefetch runs after the drop and cookieless steps, as in analytics, so it loads only teams with surviving events.
- In errortracking it runs right before the Cymbal call, so the load overlaps symbolication.
- The error-tracking server config type now picks both flags; its defaults already load them.
- `ErrorTrackingHogTransformer` now includes `prefetchHogFunctionsForTeams`.
- Mechanical: `createPrefetchStep`, `prefetchTeamsStep` and `prefetchHogFunctionsStep` move from `pipelines/analytics/steps/` to `ingestion/common/steps/`, in separate commits with no behavior change.
- Mechanical: the errortracking pipeline docstring gains both prefetch phases and renumbers the phases after them.

## How did you test this code?

- The existing pipeline tests for heatmaps, clientwarnings, ai and errortracking now run with teams prefetch on, and ai and errortracking also with hog-function prefetch on. Every case checks that prefetch leaves the results unchanged.
- No new standalone tests: the step tests already cover each step's behavior, and a per-pipeline "was it called" test would only mirror the wiring.
- Ran locally: those four pipeline suites, their consumer tests, the moved step tests, and the analytics prefetch step tests.
- Not run: `errortracking/consumer.test.ts` and other database-backed suites, because the local worktree had no Postgres or Redis.
- Not labeled `test-new-events-schema`: the diff changes no event content, event reads or event-table SQL.

## Problem

The decision playground shows "The decision model could not answer this request" for every question, even though the AI gateway answers correctly. In prod-us, the last playground attempt logged `ml_inference_decision_gateway_refused` with `status_code: 200`. The gateway returned a good decision, and Django refused it.

hogference's Jev server reports `latency_ms` with two decimals (for example `41.25`). `DecisionResult.latency_ms` was typed `int`, and pydantic refuses to truncate a fraction. So `parse_result` raised on every answer, and the view turned that into a 502.

## Changes

- `DecisionResult.latency_ms` and the response serializer's `latency_ms` accept a float.
- The playground rounds the latency when it shows it.
- The logic tests' decision fixture reports a fractional latency.

## How did you test this code?

- `products/ml_inference/backend/tests` passes locally.
- With the old `int` contract, 6 tests fail on the new fixture, so it catches this regression.
- I fed an answer in the Jev server's exact shape (upstream `jevk5.prompt.answer` at the pinned commit) through `parse_result`. It failed on `latency_ms` alone.
- Not checked in the browser. The playground only renders the rounded number.

body:
## Problem

- After #105829, a full stamphog review still takes about 115s (median), against a goal of under 75s. The LLM uses about 34s of that.
- About a third of gate outcomes still miss the fast path. Most are a pending `Migration risk` check, which costs ~55s of sandbox per review for a WAIT known up front, often several times in a row on the same PR.
- The first-day check of 2.1.0 needed log scraping and timestamp joins. It still could not see inside the reviewer step, the bot wait, or the context fetch.

Measured on 2.1.0 (first ~20h, worker step timings joined with `$ai_generation`):

| Step (full review, median) | Time | Cause |
|---|---|---|
| `ship_engine` | ~11s | ~30 sequential sandbox write and exec calls |
| After the last LLM call | ~10s, flat | not the result event, which fires ~0.1s after the last call |
| Context fetch | 10–60s | a dozen GitHub reads in sequence |
| Familiarity | absent on ~1 in 6 T1 reviews | GraphQL history requests time out |

## Changes

Expected: roughly 20s off every full review, and pending-migration WAITs down from ~55s to the fast path's ~20s. Not yet seen in prod.

- **The review payload ships as one archive.** Engine, owners resolver, trusted policy and context go in one gzipped tar and one extract command. The wipe scope is unchanged: every policy path and the whole engine and owners directories.
- **The reviewer CLI's own traffic is off.** The sandbox env sets the three switches the tasks sandbox already uses (`NETWORK_RESTRICTED_AGENT_ENV`). The ~10s tail cause is inferred from the timing pattern. The new timing event confirms or refutes it.
- **The pre-check reads the PR head's `AGENT_APPROVALS.md` files.** The shared `GitHubFilesFetcher` reads them into the pre-check tree, so the size gate budgets exactly like the sandbox. This fixes misses in the band between the global ceiling and the delegation contract.
- **A pending migration check gets its WAIT without a sandbox.** It stays undecided when a dependency manifest is present, because the manifest scripts scan needs git and can add a deny.
- **Context reads run in parallel**, with per-read timings on the run.
- **Familiarity history requests are smaller** (4 paths instead of 10), and the run records why facts are missing (`familiarity_status`).
- **Every posted verdict emits `stamphog_review_timings`**, one `stamphog_timing_<step>_ms` property per step. It covers context reads, bot wait, pre-check or sandbox steps, engine phases (uv launch, gates, familiarity, LLM, flush), the exec tail and the verdict post.
- Engine version 2.2.0. The activity keeps its name and `refused` key for Temporal replay.

> [!NOTE]
> Riskiest parts: the pre-check finality rules in `review_local.py` (a wrong final verdict is never re-reviewed), and the payload wipe in `_review_payload_command`. The rest is plumbing.

Pre-check before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Context]:::phYellow --> P[Pre-check, no folder files]
  P -- final deny --> R[Refusal]:::phYellow
  P -- pending migration or size band --> S[Sandbox]:::phGray --> V[Verdict]:::phYellow
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

Pre-check after:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Context + head folder files]:::phYellow --> P[Pre-check, exact size gate]
  P -- final deny --> R[Refusal]:::phYellow
  P -- pending migration, no manifest --> W[WAIT]:::phYellow
  P -- otherwise --> S[Sandbox]:::phGray --> V[Verdict]:::phYellow
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

Not in this PR:

- **Renamed files.** The sandbox engine's `git diff --numstat` prints a rename as `old => new`, so gates see a garbled path, and the pre-check skips renames for that reason. Fixing it changes which path the deny-list sees for a moved file, which is a policy call.
- **Clone** is now the largest step (~27s). Cutting it needs a cached mirror, for example on a Modal volume, which is new infra.
- **Shared parts.** `NETWORK_RESTRICTED_AGENT_ENV` and the tar batch write could move into the tasks sandbox facade. Wizard and notebooks already hand-roll the same tar pattern.

## How did you test this code?

- The engine test for pre-check finality now covers the folder-file deny, the pending-migration WAIT, and the manifest case. It runs a full `run()` on each final case and asserts the same verdict.
- The integration test runs the real pre-check child process against the fakes. It covers a served `src/AGENT_APPROVALS.md` that lifts the ceiling (must go to the sandbox), a failed folder read, the WAIT fast path, and the recorded `pregate_outcome`.
- The existing sandbox env test now requires the three CLI switches.
- A new `main()` test pins the last-line result contract, including the engine timings.
- The familiarity failure test now asserts each status.
- The happy-path integration test asserts the timing event and its step properties.
- The real archive and extract command ran in a `debian:bookworm-slim` container. A planted shadow `yaml.py` and `steering.md` were removed, all engine and owners files landed, and `date +%s%3N` printed epoch ms.
- Not tested: a real Modal run, so the CLI-traffic cause of the ~10s tail is unconfirmed. Also untested: a real GitHub read of folder files on a private repo.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

Stamphog's README (how it runs, the timing event) and AGENTS.md (pre-check parity rule) are updated in this PR.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5 (Sonnet 5 for the four `/simplify` reviewers)

body:
## Problem

Logs users can lose the Environment facet (and the Kubernetes and Host facets) in the facet rail, even when their logs carry the key. The facet rail presence probe has two defects:

- The generated client sends `dateRange` as `[object Object]`. The server cannot parse it and uses the last hour. So a key that did not appear in the last hour hides its facet.
- The probe lists only the 100 resource keys with the most log lines. A tenant with more resource keys can lose the environment key.

**Why:** a customer asked for the Environment facet next to Level and Service, and did not see it. The facet exists and the docs are correct; the presence check was wrong.

## Changes

- The logs attributes endpoint takes an optional `keys` param (comma-separated, max 100). When set, it returns only those exact keys. A plain string arrives correctly from both the generated client and the MCP client, which JSON-encodes arrays.
- The key predicate goes next to `{where}`, not inside it. `where()` also feeds the resource-fingerprint subquery, which has no `attribute_key`. This follows `LogFacetValuesQueryRunner`.
- The presence probe asks for the 8 curated keys and aliases, derived from `FACETS` by `presenceProbeKeys()`.
- The probe window: a selection inside the last 7 days uses the endpoint default (last 7 days) and does not refetch. A selection that starts earlier is probed as-is, so keys in older logs keep their facets. Not 90 days always: the probe has no cache, runs on each Logs page mount, and 90 days can hit the 5 GB read cap on `log_attributes3`.
- The window goes out as flat `date_from`/`date_to` params, read only when `dateRange` is absent. The generated client cannot send the JSON `dateRange` without a cast. The MCP tool excludes the flat params, so agents keep one date mechanism.
- Mechanical: `LogAttributesQuery.attributeKeys` in the schema, and the generated TS, MCP zod, and MCP snapshot gain `keys`. The generated files were updated by hand because the codegen stack was not available. Please let the `build:openapi` / schema CI checks confirm them.

Overlap: [#106480](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106480) fixes only the date range, with a cast and a 90-day window. This PR also fixes the top-100 cutoff. Both PRs edit `facetPresenceLogic.ts` and add `facetPresenceLogic.test.ts`, so only one of them should merge.

## How did you test this code?

- `pytest products/logs/backend/test/test_log_values_attributes.py`: passes, against local ClickHouse and Postgres. The new `TestLogAttributesKeysFilter` tests fail without the runner change:
  - `test_keys_returns_low_volume_key_beyond_top_100` catches the top-100 cutoff.
  - `test_keys_survive_resource_attribute_filter` catches the key predicate leaking into the fingerprint subquery.
  - parsing tests cover blanks, duplicates, absent keys, an empty value, and more than 100 keys (400).
- `jest products/logs/frontend/components/LogsViewer/FacetRail/`: passes. The new `facetPresenceLogic.test.ts` mocks HTTP (MSW), not the generated client, so it goes through the real URL builder. It fails on the old probe.
- `facets.test.ts` checks that each probed key keeps a facet after `resolveFacets`, so the probe and the resolution cannot drift apart. `presenceProbeWindow` tests cover recent and older selections.
- `test_flat_date_params_scope_window` and `test_date_range_json_wins_over_flat_params` cover the flat date params. `facetPresenceLogic.test.ts` checks that an older selection re-probes with `date_from`.
- `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend typescript:check`: no errors. MCP `tool-schema-snapshots.test.ts`: passes.
- Not done: manual testing in a running app.

body:
## Problem

Anyone running Code tasks from unattended automation — a cron, an internal admin app, a script — can no longer bill those runs to their own Claude plan. Every run comes back with a 400:

> Only PostHog Desktop can start a run on your Claude plan. Start the task from Desktop, or drop this setting to use PostHog credits.

#105218 narrowed `claude_model_access: "own-subscription"` to PostHog Desktop OAuth grants. A personal API key cannot satisfy `_is_desktop_app_grant` under any configuration, so server-to-server callers are excluded by construction — there is no Desktop for a cron to start from. They silently fall back to PostHog credits instead.

The gate itself is sound. PostHog stores no Claude token: a subscription run asks the person who started it for one over the run's stream, and the run fails if nobody answers. Restricting the choice to callers that *can* answer is right. The mistake is equating "can answer" with "is Desktop".

A personal API key is a deliberate server-to-server credential. Its owner can run the same credential relay unattended — read the run's event stream, answer the `credential_request` on the command endpoint — which is exactly what internal automation does today.

## Changes

- `claude_model_access: "own-subscription"` is accepted from **PostHog Desktop grants or personal API keys**. Everything else still gets a 400, with the message updated to name both accepted callers.
- Sandbox tokens stay excluded, unchanged: they fail the Desktop check, and they authenticate with `OAuthAccessTokenAuthentication`, so they fail the personal-API-key check too. Agent code must never put a run on its owner's plan.
- Browser sessions stay excluded. Nothing in a session can answer the credential request, so the restriction still does its job there.
- Resuming without naming the choice is untouched — still sandbox-only. Every other caller names `claude_model_access` explicitly, which now passes for a personal API key.
- Mechanical: the `claude_model_access` help text and the four generated API artifacts that embed it.

Two things worth a reviewer's eye:

## Problem

Part of #104853.

- Users on the stable build (`?stable_chunks=1`) revalidate the render-blocking eager stylesheets on every page load after 60 seconds.
- Observed in production:

| File | `Cache-Control` |
| --- | --- |
| `styles-eager-tailwind-HHD5DH7J.css`, `styles-lazy-42F5B0CB0E-3TTIOPFX.css` | `public, max-age=60, must-revalidate` |
| `chunk-S5F888C5975.js`, `index-DE3U56RC.css` | `public, max-age=604800, immutable` |

- The asset upload in PostHog/charts (`charts/posthog-app/templates/posthog-django/syncHooks-upload-assets.yaml`) marks a file immutable only when it matches `.*/[A-Za-z0-9]+-[A-Z0-9]{6,}\.(js|css)(\.map)?$`.
- A dash in the part before the hash fails that rule.
- The same rule also misses stable JS copied from dashed, dotted or underscored esbuild names, for example `github-dark-S…`, `editor.main-S…` and `hogql_parser_wasm_browser-S…` (shiki, mermaid, monaco, the HogQL wasm parser).

## Changes

- Every stable-build file now has an alphanumeric camelCase stem, so the CDN caches it as immutable.
  - Split stylesheets: `styles-eager-tailwind` becomes `stylesEagerTailwind`, and `styles-lazy-<ID>` becomes `stylesLazy<ID>`.
  - Stable JS: `github-dark-S…` becomes `githubDark-S…`. Already-alphanumeric names such as `chunk`, `index` and `App` do not change.
- One helper, `alphanumericStem`, produces both kinds of name.
- Internal group names, `@css/…` import-map keys and the manifest shape do not change. The backend reads URLs from the manifest and parses no names.
- A new test mirrors the charts regex, so a name change that would lose the immutable cache fails here first.
- Widening the charts regex was rejected. It changes another repo's deploy config and does not protect this repo from the next rename.
- The Python fixture rename in `test_stable_chunks.py` is mechanical.

## How did you test this code?

- `stableAssetNames.test.ts` checks the CSS group stems and `stableFileName` for representative prefixes against the charts regex. With the old naming, 8 of its 13 cases fail.
- Full production build (`pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend build`), then the charts regex over `frontend/dist`:

| Stable output | Matched |
| --- | --- |
| JS files in the import map | 1905 / 1905 |
| Split stylesheets (`styles*.css`) | 177 / 177 |
| Their source maps | 2082 / 2082 |

- Before the fix, 187 esbuild JS names in `dist` had a non-alphanumeric stem.
- `node frontend/bin/check-eager-graph.mjs` passes.
- Ran jest over `frontend/bin` and `common/esbuilder`.
- Not run: the two database-backed cases in `posthog/test/test_stable_chunks.py`, because no local Postgres was available. The other cases pass.

body:
## Problem

Rasterized videos, which Replay Vision's model watches and cuts thumbnails from, differ from what the web player shows:

- Recordings of apps that load CSS with `<link crossorigin>` (including PostHog's own) render as raw unstyled HTML after every full snapshot. The rasterizer proxies replay-frame stylesheets and its response carried no `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so Chrome blocked them.
- Multi-tab sessions are fed into one rrweb replayer. rrweb node ids are only unique per window, so one tab's full snapshot replaces another's page, that tab's mutations land on the wrong DOM, and the footer URL can name a tab that is not on screen. The model then reports "URL and content out of sync" as a product bug.
- CJK, Thai, Indic scripts and most emoji render as empty boxes: the image only has DejaVu fonts.
- `animation: none` at high speed leaves content revealed by a keyframe stuck at `opacity: 0`.
- Sessions with snapshots but no full snapshot render an all-blank video, and retries render it again.
- The footer is small, its long URL pushes `REC_T` around, and a window switch or an idle stretch is not visible.

## Changes

- **CORS:** proxied stylesheet responses carry `access-control-allow-origin: *`. The fetch sends no credentials and the replay iframe runs no scripts.
- **Per-window playback:** one rrweb `Replayer` per recorded window, as in the web player. Playback switches to the window that owns the current segment and hands over when a window runs out of events. The frame timeline stays on the session clock, so thumbnail and citation mapping is unchanged.
- **Footer:** two rows, 80px, 22px text. Row 1 is centered at fixed widths: `REC_T`, `WINDOW: X of Y`, `STATUS: [ACTIVE|IDLE|RECORDING ENDED]`. Row 2 is the on-screen window's URL without its query string, cut with an ellipsis. The capture viewport grows by the footer height, so the recording keeps 1280x720. The rasterizer reports `footer_height_px` and thumbnails crop by it, falling back to 32px for older videos.
- **Fonts:** Noto CJK, Noto Core, Noto Color Emoji and Liberation in the rasterizer image (about +150 MB).
- **Animations:** both players take the snap-to-end rule from `replay-shared` (`speedDependentStyleRules`). The web player's behavior is unchanged.
- **No full snapshot:** `NO_SNAPSHOTS` is final when snapshots loaded but no window has a full snapshot, so Replay Vision gates the session as ineligible without re-rendering. Nothing loaded at all stays retryable.
- **Prompt and cache:** the preamble describes the new footer; the signal `url` field reads the navigation timeline's full URL. A renderer version in the render fingerprint re-renders cached videos once, so the new prompt never meets an old video.

> [!NOTE]
> Deploying the Replay Vision worker before the rasterizer is safest: a render finished by the new rasterizer but stored by the old worker loses `footer_height_px`, and its thumbnail would keep part of the footer.

## How did you test this code?

- A local harness runs the production rasterizer image against a real four-window recording with production's config. It reproduced the broken production video frame for frame (8 CORS errors, ~30 "Node not found" warnings). With this branch: no errors, every frame styled, correct window switching and footer.
- A font test page renders every previously boxed script.
- New tests: window switching by segment, handing over when a window finishes, starting inside another window's segment, an inactivity skip landing in another window, query stripping, thumbnail crop by footer height. The interceptor test asserts the CORS header.
- Not checked: scroll restoration after a switch in a real recording, and memory on sessions with many tabs (every window's replayer is built up front).

- [ ] Publish changelog?

None.

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5

body:
## Problem

A team's daily experiment results publish hours after their configured recalculation time. The two hourly workflows compute every metric for every team in the hour first (2.5h+ on the big EU batches) and only then publish, so the earliest-finished experiment waits for the slowest one. A mid-batch worker restart also loses the publish for the whole hour, which is how the daily publish silently vanished for one batch on Sep 22.

```
before:  compute all metrics (whole hour, hours) ──barrier──> publish every experiment
after:   per experiment: compute its metrics ──> publish it (seconds later)
```

## Changes

- Each hourly workflow now groups its metrics by experiment and runs the publish activity for an experiment right after that experiment's own metrics finish. Early experiments publish minutes after the hour starts instead of at the end of the batch.
- One slow experiment, or a worker restart mid-batch, now delays or loses only its own publish; every other experiment's publish already happened.
- ClickHouse load is unchanged: all metric activities still share the same hour-wide concurrency limit (`MAX_CONCURRENT_METRICS`). The publish activity itself is a few Postgres queries (~0.7s in production).
- A failed publish (after its 3 retries) no longer relies on a gather side effect: it is caught per experiment and skips only that experiment's publish, matching the previous behavior.
- The restructure reorders workflow commands, so it sits behind a new `workflow.patched` gate and the old whole-batch path stays in the `else` branch for executions that started before the deploy. Same rollout pattern as the previous two changes to these workflows.
- Mechanical: workflow docstrings and the temporal README/ARCHITECTURE notes updated to describe the per-experiment publish.

## How did you test this code?

- New workflow test (Temporal time-skipping environment, mocked activities): a slow experiment's metric only completes after the fast experiment's publish ran, so the old whole-batch shape fails the test and the per-experiment shape passes. Verified both directions.
- Existing timeseries sync, discovery, and recalculation workflow suites pass (243 tests); the sync activity's row-sharing semantics between the two workflows are unchanged and already covered there.
- mypy and ruff clean on the changed files.

Temporal README and ARCHITECTURE notes updated in this PR. No user-facing docs describe the publish timing.

## Problem

- An engineer who sees slow Kafka produce acks cannot tell where the time goes: the client queue, the connection, or the broker.
- The image-fetch lane shows this today. Its publish acks take about 3 times as long as the WarpStream agents take to answer.
- Two causes fit: CPU throttle on the librdkafka threads, or the in-flight limit. The idempotent producer allows 5 requests in flight on each connection.
- The existing metrics show the queue size, but not whether the connections are full.

## Changes

- Producers with a name now export client-level rollups of the librdkafka per-broker stats. Labels stay at `producer_name`, so series do not grow with the broker count.
- `kafka_producer_requests_in_flight` and `kafka_producer_requests_queued` sum the requests that wait for a response or wait to be sent.
- `kafka_producer_busiest_broker_requests_in_flight` shows the connection with the most requests in flight. At 5, that connection is at the idempotent limit.
- `kafka_producer_broker_latency_seconds` reports the mean and the highest broker p99 for the internal queue, output buffer and round-trip latencies. The window is the last stats interval, and the values convert from microseconds to seconds.
- Bootstrap entries (`nodeid` -1) stay out of the rollups, the same as in the broker state count.

## How did you test this code?

- Added one Jest case in `kafka-producer-metrics.test.ts`. It catches a rollup that counts bootstrap entries, averages per broker instead of per sample, or skips the microsecond conversion.
- A mutation check confirmed the test has teeth: with the bootstrap exclusion removed, the new case fails (in-flight 107, expected 7).
- Not checked: the live stats payload of the librdkafka version in production. The field names come from librdkafka `STATISTICS.md`, and every new schema field is optional.
- Event-table coverage: this diff does not touch event ingestion or event reads, so it has no `test-new-events-schema` label.

## Problem

Someone who watches the PostHog bot expand a link in Slack has no way to learn it also answers questions about that resource.

Every other PostHog-authored Slack surface already invites a follow-up: scouts, the inbox, subscriptions, exports and eval reports. The unfurl is the only one that does not.

body:
## Problem

Opening a trace by id with no date bound is slow. `trace_id = X` on `trace_spans` makes ClickHouse load the per-part `idx_trace_bloom_part` filter for every part that matches the team. That index has one filter per part, sized by the part's distinct trace ids, so the lookup reads every filter in retention.

The existing `projection_index_trace_id` (`SELECT _part_offset ORDER BY trace_id`) can answer `SELECT _part, _part_offset ... WHERE trace_id = X` without opening the main table. But HogQL adds `team_id = X` to every table reference, and `team_id` is not in that projection, so a HogQL query can never be answered from it.

## Changes

- Adds copies of the two `trace_spans` index projections that lacked `team_id`, now storing it, in every environment, through the base `roles/logs/traces` HCL layer:
  - `projection_index_team_trace_id`: `SELECT team_id, _part_offset ORDER BY trace_id`
  - `projection_index_team_span_id`: `SELECT team_id, _part_offset ORDER BY span_id`

  Both use the table's default index granularity. The existing `projection_index_trace_id` and `projection_index_span_id` stay. Every other projection in the schema already selects or groups by `team_id`.
- `team_id` is stored, not sorted on. IDs are globally unique, so a team-scoped lookup reads the same granules as it would with `ORDER BY team_id, <id>`. With the id as the only sort key, a lookup by id alone (no team) can still use the projection. So these projections can later replace the old ones.
- Goldens, generated SQL, the Python DDL, and the local dev script are updated to match.
- Migration `0333` only runs `ADD PROJECTION IF NOT EXISTS`. The generator also emitted `MATERIALIZE PROJECTION`, which was removed: **the new projections are not materialized.** Parts written before the migration never get them and age out with retention. Until then, lookups on those parts fall back to the main table.
- Migration-only, per the ClickHouse migration rules. The query change that uses the projection is stacked on top in #106171.

## How did you test this code?

- `posthog/clickhouse/hcl/check.sh` passes (composition, goldens, SQL freshness, duplicates baseline). `diff.sh` shows two `ADD PROJECTION` statements on the logs role of local-multi, local-single, dev, prod-us and prod-eu, and no unsafe statements.
- `test_schema.py` (trace_spans snapshots updated) and `test_migrations.py` pass.
- On a local two-node ClickHouse 26.6.2.158 cluster with synthetic data, the team-scoped `_part` subquery was answered from this projection on both shards, with no skip index time. Not checked on dev or prod data.
- New events schema: not applicable, no event-table change.

- [x] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->

## Problem

Experiment metrics recalculate once per day per team. A customer wants results refreshed twice a day, and the single `experiment_recalculation_time` column cannot hold a second time.

## Changes

- Adds `experiment_recalculation_times` to `TeamExperimentsConfig`: a list of `"HH:00:00"` UTC strings, at most 2 entries, distinct, at least 6 hours apart (circular, so 23:00 and 01:00 count as 2 hours). Includes a backfill from the legacy column.
- The `experiments_config` serializer validates the list and keeps both columns in sync: writing either one updates the other.
- Nothing changes for users yet. The hourly workflows still read the legacy column; the read path and the flag-gated UI come in follow-up PRs.

Design notes:

- A list column instead of a second time column, so raising the cap later is a serializer constant change, not a migration.
- Entries must be on the hour because scheduling is hour-granular (24 hourly Temporal schedules). The legacy column silently ignores minutes; the new field rejects them instead.
- The write path ships before the read path so there is no deploy window where new code reads a column old code does not write.

## How did you test this code?

- Extended the `experiments_config` tests in `test_project.py`: a sync round-trip test (catches dual-write drift, which would make recalcs run at the wrong hour) and parameterized reject cases (sub-hour times the scheduler would ignore, overlapping times, too many entries, empty list).
- `sqlmigrate` confirms the migration is a plain nullable `ADD COLUMN` on the extension table.
- Not tested: the backfill migration (trivial hour extraction on a small table).
