body:
## Problem

- A scheduled broadcast can't be stopped or edited from Broadcasts. Once launched it stays read-only until it sends.
- A relaunched broadcast can silently never send. Editing the audience of a draft pauses its schedule, and launch cannot resume a paused one (schedule `status` is read-only in the API). The flow goes active, the toast says "Broadcast scheduled", and nothing fires.
- Follow-up to [#106363](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106363), whose review flagged both: the lost stop control ([thread](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106363#discussion_r4099291459)) and the paused schedule ([thread](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106363#discussion_r4099800863)).

## Changes

- A live broadcast with a send still to come gets "Stop and edit" on its summary. It confirms, sets the broadcast to draft and opens the wizard on the review step.
- A broadcast that already sent once ("send now", or a one-time schedule that fired) gets no button, since relaunching it would email everyone again.
- A workflow with more than one schedule gets no button either. The wizard models one schedule, so a relaunch would fold them into one.
- The button waits until the runs load, and stays hidden while any run is unfinished or when the wizard can't edit the graph, including a broadcast's own graph edited elsewhere.
- The schedule stays on the draft so the wizard still shows its timing. The scheduler already skips a flow that isn't active.
- Launch now replaces every existing schedule with a fresh one after the audience preview.
- The new schedule is created and the old ones deleted while the broadcast is still a draft. Activation comes last, so a failure part way never leaves two live schedules or none. This also stops an old schedule firing when someone relaunches with "Send now", and covers workflows with more than one schedule ([thread](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106363#discussion_r4099800871)).
- Stopping can race the scheduler. The scheduler checked the flow status in one transaction and created the batch job in another, so a stop committed in between still sent.
- The scheduler now creates the job only if the flow is still `active` under a row lock. A stop that commits first wins. A stop that commits after finds the job, and "Stop and edit" cancels any run still unfinished once the flow is a draft, with a warning that emails already sent aren't recalled.
- The relaunched schedule keeps the old schedule's variable overrides. The wizard has no variables step to set them again.
- This is the only backend change: `process_due_schedules` in `hog_flow.py`, with a regression test that flips the flow to draft between the status check and the job insert.
- `canMoveToDraft` is a pure function next to `canEditInWizard`, with test cases for each state.

![bcast-draft-1-scheduled-summary](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/ba85e5c8d62dbece5980de55ab9e090080ed5c89/2026/09/586dafea-b57f-4114-9d9f-ae2b41030070.png)
![bcast-draft-3-wizard-review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/560ba614919bceb8f892a599c66c36d911cc3da7/2026/09/1798d136-02cc-4fa7-8aad-dc7204d4ba29.png)
![bcast-draft-6-sent](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/f0754e04761b0d46078dce8d2886c83224caa82f/2026/09/0e144aa9-f835-4260-ba15-c07c5e05bf38.png)

## How did you test this code?

Playwright against a local stack, with Postgres read after each step.

| Step | Master | This branch |
|---|---|---|
| Scheduled broadcast, "Stop and edit", confirm | No button | Wizard opens on review, flow `draft`, schedule kept |
| Edit the audience, continue | Schedule `paused` | Schedule `paused` |
| Launch | Flow `active`, schedule still `paused` | Old schedule row deleted, one new `active` schedule |

- Scheduler, schedule forced due: while the broadcast was a draft, `process_due_schedules` skipped it and created 0 batch jobs. Once active again it fired 1 (cancelled straight after).
- Sent right away (no schedule), and a one-time schedule that already fired: no button.
- Weekly on Mondays, started two weeks earlier, one run done: "Stop and edit", then a due schedule on the draft created no job. The relaunch wrote `FREQ=WEEKLY;INTERVAL=1;BYDAY=MO` from the same start, and the scheduler set the next run to the coming Monday with no catch-up send.
- A workflow with a fired one-time schedule plus an active weekly one: no button. With only the weekly one left: "Stop and edit".
- Send running, and a workflow with a custom recipient: no button.
- Launch where creating the new schedule fails (simulated 500): error toast, broadcast stays draft, old schedule kept.
- Launch where deleting the old schedule fails (simulated 500): broadcast stays draft with both schedules, so nothing fires.
- Retry after both: broadcast active with exactly one schedule.
- Runs request held open: no button until it returns.
- An older run still queued behind a finished one: no button.
- Stop racing a send: a queued run inserted in Postgres as the stop request goes out gets cancelled through the real cancel endpoint (200), and Postgres reads the run as `cancelled`. The toast warns that sent emails aren't recalled.
- Schedule variables: a schedule with `{"greeting": "kept"}`, stopped and relaunched, comes back with the same variables.
- The scheduler change is covered by the new pytest, which flips the flow to draft between the status check and the job insert and finds no job. Not run through the live local scheduler, because the local server runs master's backend.
- The audience preview is stubbed, because it returns 500 on this local stack.

Not tested: relaunching in "Send now" mode, because the stubbed preview token can't create a real batch job.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

None.

body:
## Problem

- The broadcasts list shows 100 rows at a time with no way to find one by name, status or creator.
- Each row loads its latest run and metrics, so 100 rows fire hundreds of requests before the status chips settle.
- A sent broadcast can read as "Scheduled" in the list. The chip falls back to "Scheduled" while the row's runs load, and stays there if its metrics query fails.

## Changes

- The list now has a search box, a status filter (All, Active, Draft, Archived) and a "Created by" filter, matching the workflows list.
- A page now holds 30 rows, the same as workflows.
- Search, status, creator and page live in the URL, so a reload or a shared link keeps them.
- Search debounces typing by 300 ms. The loader drops a response that a newer request superseded.
- Any filter change goes back to page 1.
- The table shows its loading state until rows for the current filters arrive. If that load fails, it drops the old rows and says so.
- A row lookup from an earlier load can no longer change a newer load's rows.
- A page past the end (a stale link) lands on the last real page.
- The search box and the URL both cap the search at 200 characters, the API limit. A longer term used to show two error toasts and keep the old rows.
- A filtered list with no matches shows "No broadcasts match these filters" instead of the first-run "No broadcasts yet" call to action.
- A row's status now shows "…" until its runs load, instead of "Scheduled".
- A row whose runs fail to load on a later refresh shows "…" instead of its old status.
- The row stores its latest run before loading metrics, so a failed metrics query leaves the status correct and only the counts unknown.
- The status filter uses the workflow status. Scheduled, Sent and Failed come from each row's runs on the client, so they can't be filtered on the server yet.

![bcast-search-2-search](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/348c8876eb1e12c95da45f9d705502c6d9285ed8/2026/09/987d4399-16dc-45ae-8c0b-da909baf1d35.png)
![bcast-search-3-created-by](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/f3c50a91aa4cb384d18730ff812a5493f81367a5/2026/09/960a08b7-1841-4f72-bb60-0133b130e8c0.png)
![bcast-search-4-no-match](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/9d31c75e1cd121774abcef732b0a581c18c4a404/2026/09/ceb5d068-bc7a-4ed8-9257-9179d2f61cb9.png)

## How did you test this code?

Playwright against a local stack, with three fixture broadcasts: a draft, an active one, and an archived one named with emoji and accents and owned by a second user.

- Default load: 30 rows, pager reads "1-30 of 405", request carries `limit=30`.
- Next page: `?page=2`, 30 rows.
- Typing a search: one list request after the debounce, URL carries `?search=`, only the three fixtures match.
- Status Draft, then Archived: each shows only the matching fixture.
- "Created by" the second user, combined with search: only the archived fixture.
- Reload with filters in the URL: the search box and rows come back.
- Emoji and accented search from the URL: matches.
- 300-character search: input stops at 200, no error toast, the no-match text shows, no first-run call to action.
- `?page=abc&status=bogus`: falls back to page 1 and All.
- Status, with the metrics query forced to fail: master reads "Scheduled" for a sent broadcast, this branch reads "Sent".
- Status, with the runs request delayed 8 seconds: master reads "Scheduled" while loading, this branch reads "…", then both read "Sent".
- `?page=999`: lands on `?page=14`, the last page, with its rows.
- A 250-character search in the URL: the box holds 200 characters and no error toast shows.
- Typing a search: the table shows its loading state during the debounce.
- An older load held open 1.2 seconds lands during a newer change's debounce: the table stays loading, then shows the newer results.
- The list request failing on a filter change: old rows are dropped and the table reads "Couldn't load broadcasts". The next change recovers.
- Clearing a no-match search while the reload fails: the table and filters stay, with the load error. Master showed the first-run "No broadcasts yet" screen and hid the search box.
- Runs request failing after an earlier successful load: the row reads "…".

body:
## Problem

- The scoring sweep that would order the Self-driving inbox has nowhere to get its models from, so the ranking work behind [#106137](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/106137) cannot start.
- The training dag writes every candidate to the dedicated dataset bucket. The Temporal workers that will run the sweep have no credential for it, and granting one stalled the previous attempt.
- Both sides already reach the deployment's own object store, so that is where the models and the serving decision belong.

Closes #106454

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d77f-d7a0-7307-b991-1afc27cf9988 -->
## Origin

- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-09-25
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0d77f-d7a0-7307-b991-1afc27cf9988)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d77f-d7a0-7307-b991-1afc27cf9988 -->

## Changes

- The dag now decides what a scoring pass runs, and says so in one small JSON object the sweep reads. It is the only place that knows every family's candidate and champion at once.
- A new asset, `inbox_ranking_serving_manifest`, runs after the champion asset on every partition.

Layout in the app object store, under the existing dataset key prefix:

```text
<prefix>/serving/models/<model_name>@<model_version>/metadata.json + <head>.ubj
<prefix>/serving/manifest.json
```

| Role | Entry | Why it is scored |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `served` | champion of `INBOX_RANKING_SERVED_FAMILY` | the scores the inbox would order on |
| `daily_candidate` | that family's candidate for the partition | pairs the champion against the day's fit without a second pass |
| `cross_family` | every other family's champion with a readable head | a later interleaving needs no rescoring |

- The schema, the role names and the object keys sit in `products/signals/backend/ranking/serving_manifest.py`, beside the feature contract the two sides already share. The validators run at write time, so the dag refuses a manifest the sweep could not act on: exactly one served entry, keys matching their model, unique keys, and no more entries than the `ranking_score` artefact accepts.
- Publishing order is the safety property. Every copy finishes before `manifest.json` is written, so a failed copy leaves the previous manifest and the previous models serving. A model version is immutable, so a version already in the store is not copied again.
- No family has a champion yet, so the asset writes nothing and reports the reason. Nothing changes for any user until the sweep, the model store and the serializer field land.
- Telemetry: `inbox_ranking_serving_manifest_published` per run, plus the manifest key and entry list as asset metadata.

> [!NOTE]
> Two operational steps remain before this runs in prod-us, both named in the issue: `OBJECT_STORAGE_*` credentials that can write under the serving prefix, and one training tick with `INBOX_RANKING_AUTO_PROMOTE` on to mint the first champion.

## How did you test this code?

- `pytest products/signals/dags/inbox_ranking/tests/test_training.py` and `products/signals/backend/test/test_artefact_schemas.py`, and a check that `posthog.dags.locations.signals` still resolves with the new asset in the job. Repo-wide mypy was started but had not finished when this PR opened.
- No manual run: the dag needs the dataset bucket and a Dagster deployment, neither available here.

New coverage, and the regression each group catches:

- Validator cases — a manifest with two served entries, none, a duplicate key, a key that names another version, or one over the cap. Each of these makes the sweep's `results[served_key]` read ambiguous or unresolvable, and without the write-time check it would fail per report at scoring time instead.
- Composer cases — no champion writes nothing; a candidate at the champion's own version is not added twice; a family with no readable head is left out; the cap drops `cross_family` before the paired read; a champion written before `model_kind` existed reads as `xgboost`.
- Publisher cases — a version already in the store keeps its bytes and is not re-copied, and a failed copy or a missing source object leaves the previous manifest in place. Nothing existing covered the publish order, which is the property that stops a manifest naming a model whose booster never arrived.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

The dag's `README.md` gains the serving-manifest section and the new setting; its `AGENTS.md` gains the three invariants a later change must not break.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/editing-agents-md`, `/writing-simplified-technical-english`.
- CodeRabbit CLI was unavailable in this sandbox, so the PR opens without a local review pass.
- No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "serving manifest"` found no PR for this issue.
- The manifest asset started as one function. It was split so the entrypoint stays thin and the composition is a pure function over the two `metadata.json` records, which is how the rest of this dag is tested. The publisher kept its S3 plumbing in `dag.py`, per the dag's own convention.
- Nothing here draws on non-public material: every fixture is invented from the properties each case has to exercise.

- This is layer 6, the top of the friction stack, on top of #106447.

## Changes

- The column shows a figure only for teams with at least 3 scored members, so one or two people never read as a team's figure.
- The team page gains a **Friction** section above the date panel, like the author page: the team median and its members by friction. It reads a fixed 30-day window, and the section note says so.

## Problem

- The PostHog Desktop review pane shows only one file of a multi-file PR, and "Refresh diff" does not help. Raised in a Slack thread (linked below).
- A file diff draws nothing until the syntax highlighter is ready, so every row measures 0px on first render.
- virtua drops 0px rows from its render range, so they unmount and never measure again.
- Only the row at the boundary (the last file) stays mounted.
- Since #98930 the worker pool starts cold when the review opens, so the review hits this on almost every open.

## Changes

- Every file in the review now renders. Before, a 26-file PR showed only the last file.
- Each list row has a minimum height of one file header (`REVIEW_LIST_MIN_ITEM_SIZE`), so virtua never sees a 0px row.
- Mechanical: removed the `pb-2 last:pb-0` classes. virtua wraps each row in its own element, so `last:` always matched and the padding never applied. Rendered rows look the same.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![before-review](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/8c45529d4b5ef2373ee312c15b910cd555e10cf9/2026/09/5caf52d0-304f-49f2-8533-dc390c99e6de.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/39857149cf568b3bbb54630d3ee23fbf0683b160/2026/09/c07b4604-c6bf-45ad-a279-6a99f32051f7.png) |

## Problem

- Other products cannot react to a finished task turn without the tasks product importing them.
- They also have no facade read for a conversation's full history, and no safe way to write their own key into the shared task state.
- Layer 2 of 9 in the stack that replaces #101991. The turn suggestion backend in layer 5 uses all three.

## Changes

Nothing is user-visible. The riskiest part is the lock change in `Task.mutate_state_atomic`; the rest adds new reads.

- **Turn-completed signal:** the proxy callback, the event ingest and the sandbox relay all call one `dispatch_turn_completed`. It sends a `task_run_turn_completed` Django signal, then the push notification.
- **Push failure:** a failed push notification no longer stops the signal. The interactive-mode checks moved from the push dispatcher into `dispatch_turn_completed`.
- **History read:** `read_task_run_history` returns every frame across the run's resume chain. It merges the logs with live stream entries the logs do not cover yet.
- **Size cap:** the history read returns `None` before any download when the logs are over `max_bytes`.
- **Trimmed streams:** an id-less stream stands in for the run's log only below the 5,000-entry cap, because a stream at the cap may have lost its head.
- **Duplicate frames:** a persisted server notification sits in both stores without an id. The merge keeps one copy.
- **State helpers:** `read_task_state_entry` and `update_task_state_entry` read and merge one key of `Task.state`.
- **Lock:** `Task.mutate_state_atomic` holds the row lock for the merge and hands the mutator a deep copy, so a nested edit is saved. It uses `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`, so it does not wait on the `KEY SHARE` lock that every task run write takes on the task row.
- **Existing writers:** the Slack PR and PR-ready email markers now go through `mutate_state_atomic`, with the same behavior.
- **Server notifications:** `publish_task_run_stream_notification` publishes through `TaskRun`, so the frame gets presence gating and the ACP envelope. It returns whether the live stream and the log each received the frame.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_turn_completed.py` catches a regression where a failed push notification swallows the signal, or where a non-interactive run fires it.
- `test_facade_stream_notifications.py` catches a publish that skips the log or the live stream, a duplicated server notification, and a trimmed stream that replaces the log.
- `test_models.py` catches a nested in-place state edit that is never saved.
- One test in `products/tasks/backend/tests/test_api.py` also fails on master, so it is not caused by this layer.

body:
## Problem

People drop out of realtime cohorts with person property conditions after they send an event without a person profile.

* Events captured with `$process_person_profile: false` for an existing person reach the cohort pipeline with the real `person_id` and `person_properties` set to `{}`.
* That `{}` is a placeholder from ingestion, but the processor reads it as the person's current properties.
* A condition such as `email is set` then turns false, and the person leaves every cohort that needs it.
* The person comes back only with a normal event that has a newer timestamp. For people whose traffic is mostly server side personless events, that can take hours.
* For a distinct ID with no person at all, the processor also creates a person record. That record can match cohorts with a negative person condition.

## Changes

* The cohort event shuffler now sends `person_properties` as null for events whose `person_mode` is `propertyless` or `force_upgrade`. Events with `full` keep their payload.
* The processor already reads a null payload as an event with no person data. It leaves the person record untouched and still counts the event for behavioral conditions, so no processor code changes.
* One exhaustive match on `person_mode` makes the decision, so a new mode fails to compile until someone handles it.
* A new counter, `shuffler_events_person_payload_dropped_total`, counts these events by `person_mode`.
* The fix goes in the shuffler because only the shuffler sees `person_mode`.
* A processor check for `{}` would be wrong. A `full` event with `{}` describes a real person with no properties, and `email is set` must turn false for them.
* This PR does not add `person_mode` to the event envelope, because that touches four crates and only the shuffler needs the value.

Limits and rollout:

* Error tracking events arrive as `full` even when their person lookup misses, and then carry `{}`, so they can still flip conditions.
* Personless events no longer refresh the person record, so with `COHORT_PERSON_RECORD_TTL_DAYS` set, a person with only personless traffic past the TTL loses the record.
* A cohort that pairs a behavioral condition with a negative person condition can then drop that person.
* Deploy order does not matter, because an old processor already handles a null payload correctly.
* People whose last event before the deploy was personless stay out until their next normal event. A person backfill of each realtime cohort with person conditions restores them sooner.

## How did you test this code?

* A shuffler unit test covers all three modes. It fails if personless events keep their payload, or if a `full` event with `{}` loses it.
* A new `person_record_fold` test sends a matched person a null payload event, then an older full event. It fails if the null event changes the record or makes the older event stale.
* The mixed cohort test in `stage1_worker` now also runs with a null payload. It fails if an event without person data loses its behavioral match.
* Each test failed against a deliberately broken version of the fix.
* The full shuffler suite, the two processor test files above, clippy and fmt ran locally.
* Not run: the rest of the processor suite, and anything against a live stack or real events.
* No `test-new-events-schema` label, because nothing in the diff reads events through SQL or Django.

## Release status

## Problem

* Feature flags treat some real members of a new or edited realtime cohort as nonmembers, for the whole length of the cohort's window.
* Those people did the qualifying event only earlier on the day of the save, before the stream processor started counting the new condition.
* The backfill seeder scans only the days before the boundary day, the local day of the run's `boundary_at`, so nothing ever counts that morning.
* The cohort still reads as ready, and the parity tool files these misses as an expected gap.

## Changes

* A saved cohort still becomes targetable by flags after about 17 minutes, as today. The members it missed now join shortly after the team's next local midnight.
* The seeder plans the boundary day as a trailing chunk, held until the day ends in the team's time zone plus a grace period.
* It also plans the next day when `boundary_at` plus the processor's catalog load lag crosses midnight.
* A tile scanned after its day ends holds the full count for that day. The processor merges day tiles with `max`, so the late tile never double counts what the live path saw.
* `SeedDomain` now refuses any day that has not ended at scan time, which replaces the old "before the boundary day" rule.
* Readiness ignores trailing chunks, so the move to `reconciling`, reconcile dispatch and the exhausted chunk check consider only earlier days.
* The finalizer stamps readiness as before, then moves a run with an unconfirmed trailing chunk to a new `trailing` status. The seeder completes the run once those chunks confirm.
* `trailing` is not an active status. The stall alert covers every active status and would fire daily on runs that wait for midnight.
* A trailing run holds no uniqueness slot, because tiles are keyed by condition hash and merge with `max`. The tradeoff is that no gauge, inventory or cancel command sees a stuck trailing run, and its cohorts keep today's gap.
* `compare_cohort_membership` counts the boundary day as a seed day once its trailing chunk confirms, so a miss there fails the check.
* Migration 0015 adds a nullable `claimable_after` column to `cohort_backfill_chunks`. Two seeder settings set the timing, `SEEDER_LIVE_TRACKING_LAG_SECS` (420 s) and `SEEDER_TRAILING_DAY_GRACE_SECS` (1800 s).
* The backfill inventory and the cohort page progress bar count only the chunks readiness waits for. The processor and the charts do not change.
* Mechanical: the seeder's test DDL fixture moves to 0015, and test call sites wrap day lists in `historical(...)`.

Run lifecycle before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A([awaiting_boundary]) ==> S[seeding] ==> R[reconciling] ==> C([completed])
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    class S,R phBlue;
    class A,C phYellow;
```

Run lifecycle after:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A([awaiting_boundary]) ==> S[seeding] ==> R[reconciling]
    R ==>|stamped, nothing held| C([completed])
    R ==>|stamped, trailing day held| T[trailing]
    T ==>|trailing chunks confirmed| C
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    class S,R,T phBlue;
    class A,C phYellow;
```

Runs that are seeding at deploy gain their trailing chunks on the first tick. Runs already reconciling or completed keep today's gap until it ages out.

## How did you test this code?

* Seeder unit tests pin the planning horizon, the hold at local midnight plus grace across DST, and the refusal of an unfinished day.
* A Postgres test holds a trailing day until its hold lapses, then claims it from a `trailing` run, heartbeats it, and completes the run.
* Postgres tests show that the reconcile transition, the dispatch probe and `chunk_progress` ignore a held chunk.
* A Postgres test shows that an exhausted trailing chunk fails its run only once the run is `trailing`.
* Django tests cover the finalizer's choice between `trailing` and `completed`, and parity on a confirmed boundary day.
* Django tests show that the inventory and the progress bar ignore a held chunk.
* Breaking each guarded behavior on purpose, 18 breakages in all, made at least one new test fail every time.
* Not run: the end to end drill on the dev stack. It saves a cohort midday over existing events, waits past local midnight, and confirms that a person with only morning events becomes a member.

* [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users
* [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone
## Docs update

No.

## Problem

- Most signed-out pages have no way to move from a report-only CSP to an enforced one. Only login, signup, password reset and email verification can.
- Both flags that enforce the app policy today are at 100%, so they no longer control a rollout.

## Changes

- Signed-in users on PostHog Cloud now always get the enforced app policy. Nobody sees a difference, because `csp-enforce-app-policy` was at 100%.
- Login, signup, password reset and email verification now always enforce it for signed-out visitors. `csp-enforce-signed-out-pages` was at 100% there.
- A new flag, `csp-enforce-other-signed-out-pages`, controls every other signed-out page. Each page load draws its own bucket, as before.
- The new flag starts at 0%, so those pages stay report-only, with `frame-ancestors` enforced as today.
- The new key avoids a trap in reusing `csp-enforce-signed-out-pages`: that flag is at 100%, so every signed-out page would enforce at deploy, with no ramp.
- Embeddable documents, such as shared dashboards and the exporter, stay report-only.
- Self-hosted installs stay report-only, as before. The flag never resolved there, and their violations reach nobody, so enforcement would break pages without a signal.
- Local development now enforces the policy, so a change that breaks it shows up before review.
- Every app policy report now reaches project 2. The report URL drops `sample_rate`, and the endpoint keeps a report without one. Before, staff reported at 1 and everyone else at 0.1.
- Two edge cases now follow the rules above instead of staying report-only: a signed-in user with no `distinct_id`, and a response with no `request.user`.
- Mechanical: the CSP section of `.agents/security.md` describes the new rules. The staff sampling test is gone with the staff sampling.

> [!NOTE]
> CSP report counts rise by up to 10 times at deploy. A CSP audit window that crosses the deploy shows that rise, not new violations.

> [!WARNING]
> After this ships, only a revert and a deploy can turn enforcement off for signed-in users or the listed signed-out pages. Keep the two old flags until the deploy finishes in US and EU. Pods on the old code still read them, and a revert lands back on them.

## How did you test this code?

- `test_page_is_enforced` fails if signed-in users or the listed signed-out pages go back behind a flag. It also fails if other signed-out pages read a different flag key.
- `test_other_signed_out_page_stays_report_only_without_the_flag` fails if a page outside the list, such as `/loginfoo`, enforces without the flag.
- `test_a_request_without_a_user_follows_the_signed_out_rules` fails if the code reads `request.user` directly. A response from a middleware that runs before authentication has no user.
- `test_no_endpoint_still_sends_the_policy_but_asks_for_no_reports` now fails if a self-hosted install enforces, or if local development stops enforcing.
- `test_html_response_declares_default_reporting_endpoint_with_distinct_id` now fails if the app policy's report URL carries a sample rate.
- The existing request tests now read the app policy from the enforced header for signed-in pages, and log out for the frame-ancestors-only case.
- Ran `hogli test posthog/test/test_csp_middleware.py` locally.
- Not checked: a browser against a running stack.

## Problem

The Linux terminal shares the webapp's main thread, so CPU emulation and Doom rendering compete with the rest of the interface.
The existing v86 scheduler worker only schedules ticks; the page still executes the VM.

## Changes

The terminal now runs Linux and renders Doom in a dedicated worker, leaving the page available for the webapp.

- An OffscreenCanvas keeps framebuffer rendering inside the worker, avoiding frame copies through the page.
- Messages carry keyboard, mouse, batched serial output, and filesystem requests between the page and worker.
- The page retains filesystem mounts, authenticated API calls, and write confirmations.
- Stopping the terminal terminates its worker; startup failures show a restartable error.

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Page["Main thread: UI, filesystem, Linux, Doom"] --> API["PostHog API"]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    class Page phBlue;
    class API phRed;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Worker["Worker: Linux and Doom canvas"] <-->|Messages| Page["Main thread: UI and filesystem"]
    Page --> API["PostHog API"]
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    class Worker,Page phBlue;
    class API phRed;
```

Local Chromium samples using the same VM assets and an isolated runtime harness:

| Measurement | Main-thread VM | Worker VM |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Main-thread task time during 10 seconds of Doom | 7.280 s | 0.020 s |
| CPU loop: 3 million awk additions | 14.360 s | 15.871 s |
| 100 filesystem reads of a 54 KB file | 0.906 s | 0.903 s |

These samples show the tradeoff: much less main-thread work, with about 11% slower execution in the CPU sample.
They are local measurements, not cross-browser performance guarantees.
The included [Doom benchmark](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/blob/experiment/terminal-worker/frontend/bin/bench-terminal.mjs) also measured 19 ms of main-thread work over 10 seconds in Storybook.

The appearance stays unchanged. This screenshot shows the worker rendering Doom during gameplay:

![terminal-worker-gameplay](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/ddbb3f2e8a6efe0676ad278eae9b32d82a9c29e8/2026/09/9938737e-11e7-4662-b2ce-7b007ff9bcd8.png)

## How did you test this code?

- Playwright drove the real Storybook VM: Doom movement and firing, notebook saves with confirmation, and layouts at 1280 and 800 pixels.
- Browser checks covered stopping during startup, restarting, and displaying an error when the worker script fails to load.
- Focused Jest tests protect startup cancellation, concurrent filesystem replies, reused request tags after cancellation, and worker errors and timeouts.
- Validation ran the frontend typecheck, formatting, worker build, and CI preflight.

The framebuffer path uses the real-browser checks above because unit mocks cannot validate v86 rendering.
Firefox and Safari remain unchecked; this implementation requires worker OffscreenCanvas support.
Native-JSON event coverage does not apply: the diff changes VM plumbing, without changing event queries or ingestion.

## Problem

- In local dev, a team moved to a `flag_evaluations` mode shows an empty flag Usage tab.
- Production ingestion writes `$feature_flag_called` events to the `flag_evaluations` table for every team. Local ingestion never does, because the three settings that turn the write on are unset.

- `.env.development` sets `INGESTION_OUTPUT_FLAG_EVALUATIONS_TOPIC`, `INGESTION_FLAG_EVALUATIONS_MODE=dual_write`, and `INGESTION_FLAG_EVALUATIONS_TEAMS=*`.

- `bin/start` reads the file on the host, and inside the sandbox container, where `bin/start --phrocs` starts the stack.
- CI and the Node test suites do not read the file, so the mode stays `disabled` there.
- A running stack picks this up after a restart. `.env.local` can still override each value.

## Problem

- #105785 lists ordinary workflows shaped like a broadcast on the Broadcasts page, but clicking one opens the workflow editor, not the broadcast page.
- A broadcast's summary also has an "Open in workflow editor" link that sends people out of Broadcasts.

## Changes

- A tagged workflow opens on the broadcast page. A sent or scheduled one opens the summary.
- A tagged draft opens in the wizard only when the wizard can describe it: a person audience sent to each person's own email, along trigger, email, exit. Account audiences, custom recipients and unreachable email steps open the read-only summary instead.

## Problem

- A loop owner who turns on "PR created" notifications never gets one. The event is in the picker, but no code sends it.
- A loop owner also has no way to hear when a loop's pull request is merged or closed, so they have to check GitHub.
- Stacked on [#106347](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106347), which sits on [#106338](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/106338). Both of those touch the same webhook handler.

## Changes

- Loop notifications now send "PR created", "PR merged" and "PR closed" to every channel the owner turned on for them (in-app, push, email, Slack).
- The desktop loop form gets "PR merged" and "PR closed" in a follow-up PR after this deploys. Until then, the API and MCP accept the new events.
- The GitHub `pull_request` webhook queues the event after commit, only for a run that belongs to a loop and claims the PR.
- Each event goes out once per run and PR. A row-locked list in the run state stops a redelivered webhook from sending twice.
- The loop lookup is scoped to the run's team, the same as the run-terminal path, because run state is writable.
- Email dedupe now takes a `dedupe_key`. Before, the key was the run id alone, so a PR email for a run would have been dropped after the run's own email.
- Mechanical: regenerated OpenAPI types (tasks frontend and MCP) and the three MCP loop tool schema snapshots.


## How did you test this code?

Automated tests only, run locally against Postgres and ClickHouse.

- `test_webhooks.py`: opened, merged and closed PRs on a loop run queue `pr_created`, `pr_merged` and `pr_closed`. A PR on a run outside a loop queues nothing.
- `test_loop_runs.py`: each PR event goes out once per run, and a forged `loop_id` from another team sends nothing.
- `test_loop_notifications.py`: a PR email and the run's email for the same run get different campaign keys.
- The existing `test_loops_api.py` still passes with the wider event list.

`test-new-events-schema` does not apply.

## Problem

- A reader of the ProductSetup types has to skim 55 comment lines over 87 non-blank lines to find the few that say anything.
- Most of them restate the line below: `/** Display title */` on `title: string`, `/** Icon for the task */` on `icon?: ReactNode`, `/** Whether task is completed */` on `completed: boolean`.
- `TaskType` is documented twice. The second copy sits above `taskType?: TaskType` and repeats the union and its examples, so the two can drift apart.

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d590-ac20-7eb9-ad8f-821217e73808 -->
## Origin

- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-09-24
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0d590-ac20-7eb9-ad8f-821217e73808)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P1 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d590-ac20-7eb9-ad8f-821217e73808 -->

## Changes

- Deletes only the comments that restate a field name, its type, or the next line. Comment density drops from 63% to 50% of non-blank lines.
- Folds the duplicated `TaskType` block down to the one fact the union does not carry: `taskType` defaults to `'onboarding'`.
- Keeps every comment that carries behavior the types cannot show, and sharpens three of them against the code:

| Field | Kept because |
| --- | --- |
| `skipWarning` | Setting it puts a confirmation dialog in front of skipping. |
| `dependsOn` | An incomplete entry locks the task, which `SetupTaskId[]` does not say. |
| `docsUrl` | Opens in a new tab, and `getUrl` wins when both are set. |
| `targetSelector` | Drives the post-navigation highlight. |
| `requiresManualCompletion` | Switches the task between a user checkbox and action tracking. |
| `lockedReason` | Absence is what marks a task unlocked; there is no `locked` flag. |
| `SetupHighlight.pathname` | The highlight drops when the user leaves the route. |

- No behavior change. Comments only, no type or value edits.

## How did you test this code?

- `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend typescript:check` passes.
- `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend format:check` passes.
- No tests added or changed. A comment-only diff has no regression for a test to catch.
- Not manually tested in a running app, which a comment-only change does not reach.

body:
## Problem

Part of #104853.

- Returning users wait for a "does this product have data?" probe before a gated scene renders, on every visit.
- The `ProductEmptyStateGate` mounts the scene only after the product's `detect()` answers. Only logs, metrics and tracing cached that answer.
- A production trace of the data catalog showed the cost. `metrics?limit=1` took 1.46 s of server time before the scene's own requests could start, so LCP landed at 4.7 s.
- The same scene re-ran that probe after every metrics list load, because of its `recheckActionTypes`.

## Changes

- Returning users now open gated scenes without waiting for the probe. For the data catalog that removes about 1.5 s from the critical path.
- **Rechecks:** once a product's status is `has-data`, recheck actions no longer re-detect. The recheck exists to flip needs-setup to has-data after the first entity is created in a modal.
- **New `revalidateCachedHasData` option** for products whose data users can delete, or whose data sits in a retention window.
  - A cached `has-data` answer opens the gate at once.
  - Detection then runs once in the background.
  - A `needs-setup` or `waiting-for-data` answer clears the cache, so the next visit shows the empty state. It never replaces the mounted scene.
  - Failures, `null` and `unknown` keep `has-data`.
- **Plain `cacheHasData`** for data that stays once ingested: error tracking, web vitals.
- **`cacheHasData` plus `revalidateCachedHasData`:** dashboards, data catalog, product analytics, cohorts, notebooks, actions, workflows, CDP destinations and transformations, annotations, subscriptions, heatmaps, AI observability datasets, evaluations and clusters, alerts, pulse, business knowledge, data warehouse, engineering analytics, surveys, session replay.
- Storybook clears the cache between stories, so an earlier "with data" story cannot open the gate over a later empty-state story.
- The `building-product-empty-states` skill and the `ProductEmptyState` README document the new option.

## How did you test this code?

`setupDetectionLogic.test.ts` catches these regressions:

- A recheck while `has-data` re-runs the probe. This is the data catalog's repeat probe coming back.
- Revalidation blocks the gate, replaces the mounted scene, or leaves the cache in place when the data is gone.
- A team switch during revalidation clears the new team's cache instead of the original team's.
- A failed, `null` or `unknown` background check hides a scene that has data.

21 product emptyState test files now clear `localStorage` in `beforeEach`, so a cached answer cannot leak between cases.

Not checked: Storybook visual regression. The per-story cache reset was added for that ordering risk, but the stories were not rendered locally.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop and Claude Code, Claude Opus 5.5

## Problem

- A person who asks @PostHog for a change in Slack gets a "Pull request opened" card, but hears nothing when that pull request is merged or closed.
- The backend already records the outcome (run output, report status), so only the Slack thread stays out of date and keeps reading as if the work waits for review.

## Changes

- The Slack thread now gets a "Pull request merged" or "Pull request closed without merging" reply, with the same "View PR" and "Open in PostHog" buttons.
- The closed card adds a line that says to reply in the thread to try a different approach.
- The reply tags the same person as the "Pull request opened" card.
- It posts only for the pull request that the thread announced. A PR the agent replaced with a newer one stays quiet, and so do tasks that did not start in Slack.
- Each outcome posts once per pull request. A row-locked claim on the task state stops a redelivered webhook from posting twice, and a PR that is closed, reopened, and then merged still gets its merged card.
- The GitHub `pull_request` webhook only queues a Celery task after commit, so a Slack outage cannot slow or fail the webhook.
- The card is best effort. Any failure (Slack or otherwise) is logged and swallowed, the Celery task never raises, and a failed card is not retried.
- A reopened and closed-again PR does not post a second time.
- Mechanical: the opened, merged and closed cards share one helper for the PR buttons and one for who they tag (`pr_card_reply_target`).
- Mechanical: `SlackThreadContext.from_mapping` replaces the hand-built thread context in the Slack relay and the new card service.

No UI in the web app changes. The only visible change is the new Slack message.

## How did you test this code?

Automated tests only. No manual Slack test.

- `test_webhooks.py`: a merge or close of the announced PR queues the notice with the right outcome. A close of a PR the thread never announced does not.
- `test_slack_pr_cards.py`: the card posts once per announced PR, never for an unannounced PR or a task with no Slack thread, and tags the run's actor. A Slack rejection, a missing integration, or a database error returns without raising.
- `test_slack_thread.py`: the merged and closed cards reply in the thread with the right text, and keep the progress message of a run that is still working.

Ran these three files locally against Postgres and ClickHouse. `test-new-events-schema` does not apply, because the diff does not touch event reads or ingestion.

## Problem

Selecting AdRoll, AppLovin, Outbrain, or Taboola does not register interest in Marketing analytics.
The source picker uses a fixed list that misses advertising connectors and treats BigQuery selection as marketing intent.

## Changes

- Every source in the Advertising category now records Marketing analytics intent when selected, including future connectors in that category.
- Connector selection uses the Advertising category as the sole marketing-intent signal.
- BigQuery selection now records only Data warehouse intent.
- Self-managed providers keep their separate intent tracking.
- Native integration support stays unchanged. This records selection intent, before connection or sync succeeds.

No UI layout or copy changes.

<details>
<summary>Intent flow for source selection</summary>

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Select connector] --> B{Native marketing source or BigQuery?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Warehouse and marketing intent]
    B -->|No| D[Warehouse intent only]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    class A,C,D phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Select connector] --> B{Advertising category?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Warehouse and marketing intent]
    B -->|No| D[Warehouse intent only]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    class A,C,D phYellow;
    class B phBlue;
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Analysis of additional intent signals</summary>

| Candidate | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Save custom channel rules | Strong evidence of attribution work; record after successful persistence with a dedicated context. |
| Explicitly filter a paid channel or UTM campaign | Useful acquisition signal; exclude URL restoration, empty filters, filter removal, and unrelated changes. |
| Combine a campaign/channel filter with a conversion goal | Stronger evidence of marketing analysis than selecting a goal alone. |
| Connect a Marketing & email source | Potential lifecycle-marketing signal; evaluate separately from advertising connectors. |
| Open Web analytics, change dates, or view the default Channels tab | Too broad to classify as Marketing analytics intent by default. |

Web analytics restores filters through the same actions used by interactions.
A follow-up should distinguish user actions from restoration and use separate contexts for each signal.
Existing Marketing analytics dashboard interactions and settings already record intent.
This PR scopes connector-selection intent to Advertising; Web analytics signals remain follow-up work.

</details>

## How did you test this code?

Parameterized wizard tests cover advertising connectors and prevent BigQuery or a legacy source name without an Advertising category from recording marketing intent.
Unrelated categories still record only Data warehouse intent.

Local validation includes the source-wizard Jest suite, frontend lint/format, full frontend typecheck, and strict preflight.
Browser interaction was not tested.

## Problem

Alert investigations can discard an earlier usable verdict when a later model call fails. The alert may then follow its inconclusive notification setting. The report can also show zero tool calls after using tools.

## Changes

- A failed model call now keeps the latest report with a valid verdict and summary. If none exists, it stays inconclusive.
- The returned report records the actual tool count in either case.

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Model call fails] --> B[Inconclusive report]
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    class A phRed;
    class B phYellow;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A[Model call fails] --> B{Usable earlier report?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Keep its verdict]
    B -->|No| D[Inconclusive report]
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    class A phRed;
    class B phBlue;
    class C,D phYellow;
```

## Problem

The session replay image-fetch lane drains a hot registrable domain slower than its politeness limit allows, so the frontier topic falls behind.

- One registrable domain gets at most 6 concurrent jobs.
- Each job held its domain slot until Kafka acknowledged the image publish, not only until the HTTP response ended.
- In prod-us, the publish wait (admission plus delivery) was about three times the HTTP request time. So most of a hot domain's slot time went to Kafka, not to the origin.
- Also, each pod joins the batches of all its consumer members into one fetch pass. A member cannot poll again until its pass ends, so the slowest partition in the pod sets the pace for every partition in it.

## Changes

- A job now releases its registrable-domain slot when the image response is complete, before the Kafka publish.
- The worker then starts the next job, while the publish continues in the background.
- Origins see no change: at most 6 requests per registrable domain are open at one time, as before.
- The pod candidate limit still counts each job until Kafka acknowledges the publish, so the memory bound for image bodies does not change.
- A pass still ends only after all its publishes settle, so offsets still commit only after the publish.
- The new `SESSION_RECORDING_ML_IMAGE_FETCH_JOIN_MEMBER_BATCHES` flag controls the joined pass. When it is `false`, each member batch starts its own pass immediately.
- The flag defaults to `true`, which keeps the current joined pass. A charts change turns it off after the first change is measured in prod, so each change gets its own measurement.
- `IMPLEMENTATION_NOTES.md` describes both changes.

## How did you test this code?

- New `fetch-runner.test.ts` case: it holds an image publish open and expects the next fetch for the same domain to start. Against the old code, the second fetch did not start and the test failed.
- A new row in the existing wiring `it.each` checks that the flag set to `false` gives one batch per pass, with eight consumers.
- Ran locally under Node 24: the `ml-mirror-image-fetch` suites (without the DynamoDB integration suite), the image-fetch server wiring test and `consumer-v2.test.ts`.
- Not checked: prod throughput. The lane stage metrics (`ml_image_fetch_stage_duration_seconds`) and per-partition record rates will show the effect after deploy.
- Not event ingestion or event reads, so no `test-new-events-schema` label.

## Problem

- The person deletion dashboard cannot show four things an on-call engineer needs once `PERSON_DELETE_TOMBSTONE` is on: which deletion order an environment runs, how long a delete waits for Kafka before acking the tombstone queue, whether those acks fail, and what the weekly queue repair did with the rows it read.
- None of those had a metric. The mode is a setting nothing exports, the ack failure was only a log line, and the repair's counts lived only in Dagster run metadata.
- Follows #105640, which adds the weekly repair and the queue gauges this extends.

## Changes

- `posthog_person_delete_tombstone_enabled`: a gauge set from the setting when the module loads, in every process, so the configured order is visible without a delete.
- `posthog_person_deletion_mode_persons_total{mode}`: persons a profile delete attempted, by `legacy` or `tombstone` order. Incremented once per batch in the shared dispatch, so it counts on every path.
- `posthog_person_tombstone_delivery_wait_seconds{source}`: histogram of the wait for Kafka delivery inside a tombstone-order delete, observed once per request and capped at 10 seconds. `source` is `delete` or `orphan_repair`, so the repair command's waits stay separable.
- `posthog_person_tombstone_acks_total{outcome}`: `acked` counts queue rows the ack RPC cleared, from its `cleared_count`, since an ack is idempotent and a repeat clears nothing. `ack_failed` counts the persons in one call that raised. The delete now acks in calls of 1000 itself, so a failure counts exactly its call and does not stop the others.
- Four gauges next to the existing queue gauges, pushed once per weekly repair run: rows listed, dropped, confirmed and republished. Republished counts produces, and the confirmed gauge says how many then showed in ClickHouse. The three per-outcome gauges count team passes that completed; a failed team's rows are in the unresolved and failed-teams gauges.

Nothing user-visible. The dashboard change that reads these is in PostHog/grafana-dashboards.

## How did you test this code?

- Extended the existing tests rather than adding new ones. Each assertion reads the metric back from the Prometheus registry before and after the call:
  - The legacy and tombstone delete tests each check their mode's counter moved by one.
  - The tombstone delete test checks one row was acked; the ack-failure test checks one `ack_failed`.
  - The delivery-wait test checks the histogram observed once.
  - The gauge test checks all four new per-run gauges.
- Ran `test_bulk_delete_helpers.py`, `test_orphaned_ch_persons.py`, `test_delete_persons.py` and `test_person_tombstone_queue.py` locally against a fresh test database. Not run: anything against a live pushgateway.

body:
## Problem

A session recording can render a different scroll position in one browser than another, even though both received identical recording data. The merged `recording anchor diagnostic` event confirms the data path is identical: for the same recording, two browsers reported byte-identical event counts, sources, timeline start, and `base_shift_ms = 0`. That rules out the data and the anchor and points at the player's scroll reconstruction (rrweb restoring nested scroll containers), which the event-derived diagnostic cannot observe because it reads the events, not the rendered DOM.

The reported difference is not a fixed offset — it starts small and **grows as playback proceeds**. So a single first-frame reading would miss it; the divergence has to be measured across the timeline.

## Changes

- Add a companion capture `recording anchor diagnostic rendered` that reads the **actual** scroll offsets from the replay iframe, so it can be diffed against the event-derived `recording anchor diagnostic`.
- Sample **periodically from the playback loop** (`updateAnimation`), throttled to one reading per interval and capped, each tagged with `current_timestamp` / `rrweb_player_time`. Diffing the two browsers' samples by playhead shows whether the offset accumulates over time.
- Fields: `rendered_doc_scroll_y/x`, `rendered_max_scroll_y/x`, `rendered_scrolled_element_count`, `rendered_top_scroll_node_id` (from the rrweb mirror, so it lines up with `primary_scroll_node_id`), `rendered_top_scroll_y`, a bounded `rendered_scroll_samples`, plus `sample_index`, `recording_id`, `is_brave`.
- Skipped for the preview mini-player, wrapped so it can never break playback.

To use: play the same recording in two browsers, then diff the `recording anchor diagnostic rendered` samples for that `recording_id` by playhead. If `rendered_top_scroll_y` diverges and the gap widens with `sample_index`, the divergence is in the player's scroll reconstruction.

Temporary: marked with a TODO to remove the sampler and `readRenderedScroll` once the cause is found, matching the existing anchor diagnostic.

## How did you test this code?

- `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend typescript:check`: no errors in the changed file.
- `pnpm --filter=@posthog/frontend fix` (oxlint + oxfmt): clean; the only oxlint output is pre-existing import-cycle warnings on unrelated import lines.
- I (the agent) did not run the app or exercise the capture at runtime in this environment. No automated test is added: the sampler reads live iframe DOM inside the playback loop and the capture is diagnostic-only, so a unit test would assert against a mock rather than catch a realistic regression.

None.

Nothing records whether a discovery hint was appended to a result, or whether a result was empty. Context: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C27FSAW2G/p1790280651177289

## Changes

New properties on `$mcp_tool_call`:

| Property | On which calls | Values |

| `exec_learn_kind` | every `learn`, including rejected ones | `search` (`-s`), `load` (`posthog:`/`project:`), `list` (`learn skills` or bare `learn`), `describe` (`-d`), `guide` (anything else) |

Reviewers cannot see cached conversion Paths SQL changes in the existing snapshots, which cover only live calculation.
The attribution table already has cached SQL snapshots.

## Changes

- Snapshot cached Paths for campaign, source and channel breakdowns in both event schemas.
- Preserve the live snapshots and assert that each case uses the intended reader.
- Capture the SQL from merged #106275; [this snapshot-only commit](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/f04e95b4290f2326fcf496e204498eaad6a662ac) shows the before/after change.

This PR changes tests only and has no visual or runtime behavior changes.

## How did you test this code?

The complete Paths suite runs locally against ClickHouse with both legacy and JSON events, without updating snapshots during verification.
The added cases detect cached-reader SQL changes that the existing live-only cases miss.
Applying #106275 to the original baseline causes the cached snapshots to fail while the live snapshots still pass in both schemas.
The final snapshots remove the redundant aggregation and preserve the live SQL unchanged.

An earlier JSON run timed out while inserting fixtures into local ClickHouse.
The unmodified full suite passed on retry; the original timeout cause remains unconfirmed.

Production performance was not tested by this snapshot change.

## Problem

This skill ships as a file on disk to the ai-plugin (Claude Code, Codex) and PostHog Code sandboxes. Those connections have `learn` off by design, since their skills are already on disk. The skill still told the agent to read skills with `learn`, so the agent tried it and got `unknown_command`. Low volume, but a clear break, and the server already teaches `learn` to any client that has it.

Origin: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C27FSAW2G/p1790280651177289

## Changes

- The skills-store skill reads skills only through `skill-list`, `skill-get` and `skill-file-get`, which every client that gets this file can use. All mention of `learn` is removed; the command itself is unchanged.
- One line under "Discovering skills" says to call `skill-get` directly when the user names the skill.
- A CodeRabbit path rule for products/*/skills/** flags shipped skills that depend on a flag-gated, client-specific or mode-specific command, so this does not come back in another skill.

## How did you test this code?

Verified: the built skill bundle contains no `learn`. `hogli build:skills` (the command the skills release and sandbox image jobs run) and `hogli lint:skills` both exit 0. Not run: the MCP server, since no server code changed.

body:
## Problem

Terminal users must save SQL to a file before running a query.
They cannot pipe SQL into a command or enter successive queries at a dedicated prompt.

## Changes

- `hogql "select 1"` runs a query directly, and `echo "select 1" | hogql` reads SQL from stdin.
- `hogql` starts an interactive prompt that executes one query per line and stays open after query errors.
- Output defaults to Markdown, with `--json`, `--csv`, and `--tsv` alternatives.
- `--connection-id`, JSON query options, and repeatable `--field name=JSON` arguments configure the existing query API.
- `hogql --help` documents options, examples, pagination, and interactive behavior.
- Query warnings appear on stderr, preserving parseable JSON and CSV output on stdout.
- Ctrl+C cancels the query and frees the terminal to run another command.

The command uses the existing authenticated query path and blocks execution after the terminal stops or the current project changes.

Query submission closes immediately; the interruptible response read waits for results.
Cancellation aborts the HTTP request and cancels the server query in its original project.

<details>
<summary>Query interruption flow</summary>

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Guest[Shell command] --> Close[Close request file] --> Query[Wait for query]
    Query --> Queue[9P queue stays blocked during interruption]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    class Guest phYellow;
    class Close phBlue;
    class Query,Queue phRed;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    Guest[Shell command] --> Submit[Submit query] --> Read[Open response and wait]
    Interrupt[Ctrl+C] --> Abort[Abort response read and HTTP request]
    Abort --> Cancel[Cancel server query]
    Abort --> Next[Next command can run]
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
    class Guest,Interrupt,Next phYellow;
    class Submit,Read,Abort phBlue;
    class Cancel phRed;
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Terminal screenshots</summary>

Before, reproduced with the command absent from the disposable guest:
![Command unavailable](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/0ff454af3451670161bcf0311f41ee21702073c0/2026/09/75d0aff1-d6c0-4339-84a4-dbf5eef01a8f.png)

After:
![Interactive hogql prompt](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/1dd9c264bdac5299eda4696ce04a1e5cb410778e/2026/09/98067a23-de70-4f7c-847d-a82bce9b84d9.png)

</details>

## How did you test this code?

- Shell tests protect quoting, piped input, option handling, and nonzero error exits.
- Command tests cover formats, connection fields, response metadata, invalid arguments, and project-switch protection.
- Bridge tests cover warnings in all output formats and recovery after interrupting either query command.
- Cancellation tests verify that a project switch cannot redirect cancellation to a different project.
- PTY tests exercise interactive recovery after a failed query on Linux and macOS.
- Chromium exercised the Linux command, exports, help, and interactive recovery using synthetic API responses.
- Chromium also exercised Ctrl+C in the Linux VM with mocked HTTP, verifying request abortion, server cancellation, and subsequent command completion.
- Local checks included the terminal runtime tests, TypeScript, lint, formatting, and CI preflight.
- A live external database connection was not tested.
- Native-JSON coverage applies because this adds a HogQL execution entry point; the draft uses `test-new-events-schema`.

- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone

The existing `posthog-terminal` flag controls access.

body:
## Problem

When you connect PostHog to claude.ai, one shared connector serves Claude chat, Claude Code and Cowork. When that connector asks for our tool list, it does not say which of the three products it is. Our server guesses "Claude chat" and returns the chat version of the `exec` tool description, which tells the model it can run `learn analytics` to read a guide. When the model then calls `learn analytics`, that request does say which product it is (`x-anthropic-client: ClaudeCode` or `Cowork`), and the server refuses because guides were chat-only. We promise the guide in the tool list and refuse it on the call.

Verified: the connector's tool list requests arrive without the product header, and refused `learn analytics` calls arrive with `ClaudeCode` or `Cowork` in it. Inferred: that these are the same sessions, since the two requests cannot be joined.

Origin: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C27FSAW2G/p1790280651177289

## Changes

- Any Anthropic product can now read the guides. The gate in `getExecLearnCapabilities` changes from `isClaudeChatHost()` to the existing `isAnthropicClient()`, which matches the `x-anthropic-client` header for any Anthropic product, the `Claude-User` user agent, or a client name starting with `Anthropic`.
- Nothing else changes. The tool list is still described the same way, and skills gating and UI detection are untouched. Guides are static text that Claude chat already receives, so letting Claude Code and Cowork read them costs nothing.

This cannot be fixed on the tool list side: at that point the three products are indistinguishable to us. #69648 made guides chat-only because chat drops the MCP `instructions` payload. That reasoning still holds for what we advertise; this PR only stops refusing what we advertised.

## How did you test this code?

A new test in `tool-executor.test.ts` builds the tool list request without the product header and the `learn analytics` call with `ClaudeCode` or `Cowork`, with the skills flag on and off, and checks the guide is returned. It fails on master and passes here.

Local server check, running the Hono server from this branch against a local PostHog:

| Scenario | `initialize` client name, user agent | Tool list offers `analytics` guide | `exec learn analytics` with `x-anthropic-client` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Master, connector | `Anthropic/ClaudeAI`, `Claude-User` | yes | `ClaudeCode`: `Error: [exec]: Unknown learning topic: "analytics"` |
| This branch, connector | `Anthropic/ClaudeAI`, `Claude-User` | yes | `ClaudeCode`: guide returned |
| This branch, connector | `Anthropic/ClaudeAI`, `Claude-User` | yes | `Cowork`: guide returned |
| This branch, direct CLI | `claude-code`, `claude-code/2.0.0` | no | none: `Error: [exec]: Unknown learning topic: "analytics"` |

The local server force-enables feature flags, so the refusal shows as `Unknown learning topic` rather than `unknown_command`. The unit test covers both forms.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```sh
cd services/mcp && PORT=3011 pnpm run dev
# The script sends initialize, tools/list without x-anthropic-client, then
# tools/call exec "learn analytics" with the given x-anthropic-client value.
MCP_TOKEN=<local personal API key> node connector-check.mjs 'Anthropic/ClaudeAI' 'Claude-User' 'ClaudeCode'
MCP_TOKEN=<local personal API key> node connector-check.mjs 'Anthropic/ClaudeAI' 'Claude-User' 'Cowork'
MCP_TOKEN=<local personal API key> node connector-check.mjs 'claude-code' 'claude-code/2.0.0' ''
```

</details>

Not checked: a live claude.ai session against a deployed build.

- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

None.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.1

Skills: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`. CodeRabbit CLI and the PR bot both noted that a directly connected Claude Code CLI that sends the product header can now read a guide. Accepted: that is the intent.

## Problem

The alerts platform never ticks outside the dev cluster. `create_alerts_platform_tick_schedule` returns early unless `CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT` is `DEV`, so migration-time reconciliation registers nothing in US or EU.

This blocks the APM team from seeing how the platform behaves under production load before it takes real alert traffic.

Origin: https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0BRV4Y31B3/p1790260657245219?thread_ts=1790260203.613299&cid=C0BRV4Y31B3

## Changes

- Delete the region check. The schedule now registers wherever `schedule_temporal_workflows` runs.
- No replacement gate. `bin/migrate` already skips that step on hobby deploys and on local development, so registration reaches dev, US and EU and nowhere else.
- Every sibling alerting schedule registers unconditionally for the same reason: `create_logs_alert_check_schedule`, `create_schedule_due_alert_checks_schedule`, `create_schedule_due_billing_alert_checks_schedule`.
- `docs/internal/alerts-platform-temporal.md` gains a production turn-on runbook and drops the dev-only framing.
- The workers those ticks need come from PostHog/charts#16306.

Nothing user-visible changes. Delivery stops at `alerts-platform-deliver-preview`, which records what it would have sent and contacts no destination.

A deployment ticks against empty demand until somebody backfills it. Demand comes from `PlatformAlertConfiguration` rows, and the only writer is the manual `backfill_platform_alert_configurations` command. Load therefore arrives on an operator's schedule, one team at a time, rather than at deploy.

An earlier draft gated this on a new `ALERTS_PLATFORM_SCHEDULE_ENABLED` env var. That was dropped: the var would have been disposable once both regions were on, and it cost a second charts PR to flip.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Merge order: PostHog/charts#16306 first, this PR second.**
> That PR adds the three `alerts-platform-*` workers to prod-us and prod-eu. Land it, promote the workers to both prod stages, and confirm they poll before this PR goes ready.
> This PR has no env-var brake. The schedule starts ticking in both regions at whatever deploy carries it.
> If the order slips, each region produces one timed-out `alerts-platform-orchestrate` per minute until the workers arrive. It is self-healing, and the kill switch is pausing the schedule in Temporal.

## How did you test this code?

An agent wrote this PR and ran no manual or production testing.

`products/alerts/backend/tests/test_temporal_schedule.py` drops the test that asserted the dev-only guard, because that behavior is gone. The surviving test now runs under a non-DEV deployment, so reintroducing a region check fails it instead of passing silently. No test was added: the existing `already_exists`/`paused` matrix already covers the schedule policy.

`products/alerts/backend/tests/` ran locally and is green. Not run: anything against a real Temporal cluster or a deployed environment.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

Covered in this PR.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)
**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5

Skills invoked: `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/simplify`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`.

`/writing-tests` and `/writing-code-comments` ran after the first push rather than before, which is the wrong order. `/writing-tests` confirmed the test earns its place and found no new coverage worth adding, but it did catch a stale claim in this description, now corrected. `/writing-code-comments` rejected the comment on the `CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT` override for referring to the guard this branch deletes; it now states the forward reason instead.

CodeRabbit CLI: ran once over the branch against `master`, standard policy, not `--deep`. Zero findings across all three reviewed files.

Cleanup review (`/simplify`, four parallel agents) raised three items, all fixed:

- The schedule test parametrised over `DEV`, `US` and `EU`, but the function reads no deployment setting, so the three values drove one code path and tripled the cases. It now pins a non-DEV deployment, which still fails if a region gate returns.
- The claim that registration reaches dev, US and EU "and nowhere else" did not name what it depends on. It now names `posthog-web-django` as the only chart app that enables the migration job.
- A rollback sentence restated the section above it. Removed.

The same review checked whether the gate belongs at the registry level in `posthog/temporal/schedule.py`, where `create_batch_trace_summarization_schedule` sits behind `settings.DEBUG or is_cloud()`. It does not: that gate mirrors a hard runtime precondition of the workflow, while `CLOUD_DEPLOYMENT != "DEV"` was a rollout stage written as a constant.

Known and not addressed here: `bin/docker` runs an unscoped `bin/migrate`, so a self-hosted deployment outside `docker-compose.hobby.yml` registers this schedule with no worker behind it. Every ungated sibling schedule behaves the same way there. A per-schedule exception would recreate the special case this PR removes; a fix belongs at the registry level for all product schedules.

No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "alerts platform tick schedule"` returns only the author's own delivery stack (#103180, #104842, #104857, #104862). None touches the schedule gate.

Public artifact: the work started from an internal Slack thread, linked above for origin only. Nothing from that thread reaches the diff, the commit message, or this description. No customer data, operational metrics, or quoted discussion appears anywhere in this PR.

Branch freshness: preflight reports the branch is behind master and that CI workflows changed there. Merge master in before marking ready.

Part of #104853.


## Changes

- `posthog/templates/head.html` writes `POSTHOG_APP_CONTEXT`, `POSTHOG_USER_IDENTITY_WITH_FLAGS` and `JS_POSTHOG_IDENTITY_CLAIMS` as `<script type="application/json">` data blocks.
- The existing nonce'd scripts set the same `window.*` globals with `JSON.parse(document.getElementById(...).textContent)`. The globals, their order and the `posthog-app-user-preload` id stay the same, so no frontend code changes.
- A data block is not executed, so the CSP does not apply to it.
- Django's built-in `json_script` filter renders each block and escapes `<`, `>` and `&`.
- `render_template` passes the three values as Python objects instead of pre-serialized strings.
- `json_script` encodes with `DjangoJSONEncoder`, which covers the UUIDs the removed `json_uuid_convert` handled.
- A small `page_json_script` filter wraps `json_script` with a tolerant encoder. An unserializable value renders as `null` and is reported to error tracking instead of failing the page.
- Every page that includes `head.html` picks this up: index, layout, exporter, render-query, error and two-factor pages.

Measured on a synthetic logged-in context (150 teams, 1,200 flags, 433 timezones), rendering `index.html`, gzip level 9:

| Blob | Before raw / gzip | After raw / gzip |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POSTHOG_APP_CONTEXT` | 163,587 / 20,640 | 105,934 / 19,459 |
| `POSTHOG_USER_IDENTITY_WITH_FLAGS` | 81,029 / 9,253 | 47,457 / 8,718 |
| Whole `index.html` | 251,846 / 33,446 | 160,711 / 31,442 |

## How did you test this code?

- The existing context tests now read the context values as objects. Escaping is Django's own filter, so the PR adds no test for it.
- A local render of `head.html` with `</script><script>alert(1)</script><!--` in the app context produced only `\u003C` escapes, and the block parsed back to the same value.
- In Chromium via Playwright on a local static page: the hostile page ran no script and all three globals held the exact original values; the realistic page restored 150 teams, 433 timezones and 1,200 flags.
- New `TestPageJsonScript` in `posthog/test/test_templatetags.py` renders a context holding a `set` and a UUID. It checks the set becomes `null`, the UUID a string, and one error is reported. It fails with plain `json_script`.
- Semgrep (security rules plus CI's packs) found nothing on the changed files.
- Ran locally with a temporary Postgres and ClickHouse stubbed: `test_get_context_for_template`, `test_templatetags`, `TestAutoProjectMiddleware`, the two OAuth app-context tests and `TestAccessControlProjectFiltering`. The rest of those suites need ClickHouse, so CI covers them.

## Problem

- A local dev server with a cold Vite cache skips dependency pre-bundling, so pages can fail with `Failed to resolve import`. One example is `@tiptap/extension-image` from dashboard image tiles.
- Vite's dependency scan fails on `@posthog/quill-charts`, which the Data Ops monitoring tab (`products/data_warehouse/.../MonitoringTab.tsx`) imports.
- `products/data_warehouse/package.json` does not declare the package, so pnpm never links it into the product. Every other product that imports it declares it.
- CI does not catch it. The esbuild build, TypeScript, and Jest resolve the import through the root `tsconfig.json` path mapping, which the Vite dev server does not read.
- The gap arrived with #104424, which moved the Data Ops scene into the product. A checkout keeps working while its Vite cache predates that PR.
