body:
## Problem

A ClickHouse data warehouse sync keeps failing and retrying until it exhausts its attempts when a column reported by schema discovery no longer resolves at query time ([issue](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/error_tracking/01a0d2db-bdad-7593-8a9a-c5e431b6478a)).

This happens when the synced table is a View and its underlying table had a column renamed or dropped after the View was created. ClickHouse doesn't keep a View's declared columns in sync with what it selects from, so the sync query fails with `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` (code 47). Every retry reissues the identical column list and fails the same way, so retrying only adds noise.

## Changes

- Add ClickHouse's `UNKNOWN_IDENTIFIER` error to the ClickHouse source's non-retryable errors, so the sync stops retrying and reports an actionable message telling the customer to refresh the schema or fix the affected column, instead of retrying to the max and surfacing as tracked exception noise.

## Problem The PostHog AI runner has no `/` commands, which PostHog Desktop cloud runs already support. It also drops the agent's ACP `available_commands_update` frame, so skills and `/compact` never appear. ## Changes Typing `/` in the runner composer opens a command menu: arrows move, Enter or Tab inserts `/name `, Esc closes. The menu matches the composer's width and shows about five rows before it scrolls. App commands run in the browser and never reach the agent: | Command | Does | | --- | --- | | `/good`, `/bad`, `/feedback` | Send `$ai_metric` and `$ai_feedback`, with `feedback_trigger_type: 'slash_command'`. | | `/usage` | Shows the run's token counts, context window and cost from the stream's usage snapshot. | | `/ticket` | Opens the support form in the side panel, with a link to the task. | Agent commands come from `available_commands_update`, stored in `runStreamLogic`, and go to the agent as prompt text as before. The agent gives no field that tells harness built-ins apart from skills, so a denylist hides the built-ins (`/init`, `/review`, `/model`, …) and MCP prompts, which keeps `/clear`, `/compact` and skills. Each use fires `posthog_ai_slash_command_used`, so adoption is measurable. > [!NOTE] > `/usage` shows run tokens and cost, not the AI credits that the legacy chat's `/usage` shows. Credit usage per task run needs a new backend endpoint.
How commands are discovered ```text SANDBOX (agent-server, @posthog/agent) +-------------------------------------------------------------+ | Claude adapter Codex adapter | | query.supportedCommands() skills/list + /goal | | minus its UNSUPPORTED_COMMANDS | | plus /clear | | \ / | | v v | | ACP session/update { sessionUpdate: 'available_commands_ | | update', availableCommands: [...] } | +------------------------------+------------------------------+ | v task run log (stream + logs/) | +-------------------+-------------------+ | live: SSE | reload: logs/ replay v v BROWSER (products/posthog_ai/frontend) +-------------------------------------------------------------+ | runStreamLogic.ingestAcpFrame | | isSessionUpdateAvailableCommands -> parseAvailableCommands | | -> availableCommands (latest frame wins) | +------------------------------+------------------------------+ | APP_COMMANDS (hardcoded) | agent commands btw good bad feedback | usage ticket | | /btw only on a live | | Claude run | v v +-------------------------------------------------------------+ | runSlashCommandsLogic.slashCommands = buildSlashCommands() | | app commands first, app wins a name clash | | agent: drop HIDDEN_AGENT_COMMANDS and mcp:* | | -> keeps /clear, /compact, skills | +------------------------------+------------------------------+ | v +-------------------------------------------------------------+ | TaskRunComposer -> ComposerCommandMenu | | filterSlashCommands(draft): only while draft is "/name", | | name-prefix matches first. Enter/Tab inserts "/name " | +------------------------------+------------------------------+ | user sends the draft v runSlashCommandsLogic.submitComposer (captures posthog_ai_slash_command_used) / \ app command anything else v v runAppCommand (browser) runInteractionLogic.submitComposerForm btw -> run command side_question -> user_message "/name args" -> answer card -> agent runs /clear, /compact, good/bad/feedback -> $ai_metric, or the skill $ai_feedback usage -> contextUsage -> result card ticket -> supportLogic.openSupportForm ```
## How did you test this code? - `slashCommands.test.ts`: catches a harness built-in leaking into the menu, an app command losing a name clash, and wrong filter or parse results. - `runSlashCommandsLogic.test.ts`: catches an app command sent to the agent as a prompt, a missing required argument that clears the draft, the side question request shape, and `/btw` offered on a finished run. - `runStreamLogic.test.ts`: catches the `available_commands_update` frame dropped as an unknown session update. - Stories rendered in local Storybook with a headless browser, which also checks the menu's width, its five-row cap, and that arrowing keeps the highlighted row in view. - Not checked: a live cloud run end to end. The real command list from the agent, a real side question answer, and the support side panel are not verified. 👉 _Stay up-to-date with [PostHog coding conventions](https://posthog.com/docs/contribute/coding-conventions) for a smoother review._ ## Release status - [x] No feature flag controls this change - [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users - [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone The change adds no flag. The menu shows only where the runner composer already shows. ## Automatic notifications - [ ] Publish to changelog? ## Docs update None. ## 🤖 Agent context **Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted) **Agent:** Claude Code (PostHog Desktop), Claude Opus 5.5 - The design follows the PostHog Desktop command pipeline in `products/desktop/`: client-side commands, plus the agent-advertised list with a denylist. - The person who directed the work chose the command set: the app commands plus `/clear`, `/compact` and skills. - Skills invoked: `/writing-ui-components`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`. - CodeRabbit CLI: not available in this sandbox, so the PR opened without a local pass. - No duplicate: an open-PR search for runner slash commands found nothing. - Public artifact: no session material outside this repository is in the diff or this description. --- *Created with [PostHog Desktop](https://posthog.com/desktop?ref=pr)*

## Problem

People who have not chosen a thread follow-up setting get no prompt when someone replies without tagging PostHog. This prevents them from deciding whether to send that reply to the agent.

## Changes

- An unset setting now asks the person who replied before PostHog picks up the message. Explicit choices still apply.
- The private prompt now points to the PostHog app Home tab for the threads that person starts, with plain text when this install has no app ID. The setting belongs to the thread creator, so it does not govern the thread the replier is standing in.
- The prompt says PostHog will not reply or start work without agreement, instead of promising that nothing happens at all. The classifier still reads the reply first, which is what keeps the prompt off chitchat.
- An over-quota team no longer collects a channel-visible credits notice under every untagged reply. The quota gate is the first activity in the mention workflow, so the new default sent every reply through it. The gate still stops the run, and the message waits for a mention or a confirmed reply.

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  unset[Unset setting] --> never[Never pick up]
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  class unset phGray;
  class never phRed;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  unset[Unset setting] --> ask[Ask the replier] --> consent{Consent?}
  consent -->|Yes| pickup[Pick up message]
  consent -->|No| stop[Leave it alone]
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
  class unset,stop phGray;
  class ask,pickup phBlue;
  class consent phYellow;
```

- Ran focused resolver, routing, and prompt-rendering tests. They cover unset rows, explicit choices, and the Home tab note.

## Problem

- A self-driving report built from a GitHub issue can open its implementation pull request in a **different** repository, so the issue it came from stays unfixed while an unrelated PR looks like coverage.
- The issue URL already states the repository. Selection ignored it and asked the selection agent to choose across every connected repository.
- The agent's evidence is a file-tree grep under one shared `LIMIT`. One repository can fill the result page, and a path that exists in several repositories then reads as exclusive ownership.
- Blast radius is the whole implementation chain: report target, task, branch, pull request.

Closes #105780

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d2d7-7ed5-78aa-b14e-b7836164e68a -->
## Origin

- Issues: [#105780](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/105780)
- Scout: a custom scout
- First signal: 2026-09-24
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0d2d7-7ed5-78aa-b14e-b7836164e68a)
- Likely cause: [`cf6a78e`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/cf6a78e90674dfc3e304ac4eb67c9285201dbd4e)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P1 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d2d7-7ed5-78aa-b14e-b7836164e68a -->

## Changes

- **The source repository is now an answer, not a question.** `source_repository_from_signals` reads it from the `html_url` of a report's GitHub issue signals; `select_repository_for_report` passes it to the shared selector as `pinned_repository`.
- **The selector honors the pin or stops.** In the candidate list it is returned as-is, and the agent never runs. Not in the list, the result is `repository=None` carrying the mismatch — Signals reads that as "requires human input", so nothing lands in a substitute repository.
- **Ambiguity resolves to nothing.** Issues from two repositories name neither, so selection falls back to the agent rather than guessing between them.

| Signals name | Team can reach it | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| one repository | yes | that repository, no agent run |
| one repository | no | `repository=None` + the mismatch |
| two repositories | — | agent selection, unchanged |
| none | — | agent selection, unchanged |

A pinned selection is also cheaper than it was: the agent runtime resolution and the wrong-repo corrections block are agent-only inputs, so neither is resolved on that path.

**Explicit overrides and recovery are unchanged and still win.** A reviewer's repository edit and a scout's `edit_report` both persist a `repo_selection` the activity reuses ahead of any selection. A wrong-repo dismissal already clears the selection so the next run picks again — and that run now pins correctly.

**Out of scope:** an already-persisted wrong selection is not re-derived in place. Recovery goes through the existing dismissal or repository-edit path.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only — no manual run; the selection sandbox is not reachable from this environment.

- `products/signals/backend/test/test_source_repository.py` (new). Catches a source repository silently dropped or mis-parsed: a non-GitHub signal quoting an issue link, a lookalike host, a non-string `html_url`, and two issues that must resolve to nothing rather than to whichever came first.
- `products/tasks/backend/tests/test_repo_selection_prompt.py` (extended, parameterized). Catches the pin being ignored: that an eligible pin returns without awaiting `MultiTurnSession.start` at all, that a case difference still matches, that an unreachable pin returns null naming it, and that the pin beats the single-candidate shortcut.

Ran locally after merging master: both files plus `test_repo_corrections.py` and `posthog/test/test_git.py`. `hogli ci:preflight --strict` reports no failures; `uv run mypy` is clean on the three changed modules.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

Updated `products/signals/backend/report_generation/AGENTS.md`. No user-facing docs change.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-simplified-technical-english`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/simplify`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`.
- **CodeRabbit CLI pass: not run.** Neither `cr` nor `flox` is on PATH in this sandbox, so the PR opened without a local pass. No agent review was substituted for it.
- No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "repo selection source repository signals"` found no open PR for this. #102950 is adjacent (bounding a scout's own targets), not the same failure.
- Public artifact: everything here comes from this repository and the public issue. No session-only material is in the code, tests, or this description. The test fixtures use public PostHog issue URLs only.
- The first draft added a public URL helper to `posthog/git.py`. `/simplify` found `GitHubIntegrationBase.parse_issue_url`, already the parser the other GitHub issue signal consumer uses and stricter (it requires the `issues/<number>` shape), so that rename is gone.
- Two review findings were considered and skipped, both recorded in the code. Short-circuiting the pin before the repository-cache hydration would drop the archived filter, and the pin has to agree with the agent about what is reachable. Reading the repository from a typed field on `SignalData` set at ingest is the deeper fix, but signals already ingested carry no such field, so the URL parse stays either way.
- One alternative rejected: comparing target against source again at branch/PR time. It needs a durable "was this explicitly overridden" flag the artefacts do not carry, and guessing at it from `reason` strings risks overruling a person. Deciding once, at the one stage that picks the repository, is both the root cause and the cheaper guard.

## Problem

- Two kinds of edit ran zero posthog_ai tests on the PR, so the merge queue was the first place those tests ran.
- A failure found there removes the whole batch, including PRs with no fault.
- #100145 shows the cost. It enabled two tools in feature_flags' `mcp/tools.yaml`, and Backend CI skipped on the PR. The posthog_ai check that binds `FLAG_MUTATION_TOOLS` to that yaml then failed in the queue ([run](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/actions/runs/35977679805)).

| Diff touches only | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `products/posthog_ai/eval_harness/**` | 0 products selected | posthog-ai |
| `products/feature_flags/mcp/tools.yaml` | Backend CI skipped | posthog-ai |
| `products/tasks/mcp/tools.yaml` | Backend CI skipped | tasks |

## Changes

- feature_flags gets a `backend:mcp-surface` Turbo task with `mcp/tools.yaml` as its only input. No script backs it, so it never runs anything.
- posthog_ai's `backend:test` depends on that task. Turbo then reports posthog_ai affected on a yaml change (`TaskDependencyTaskChanged`), deletions included.
- posthog_ai's `backend:test` inputs add `eval_harness/**/*.py` on top of `$TURBO_EXTENDS$`, so they cannot drift from the root list.
- tasks' `backend:test` adds `mcp/tools.yaml` as an input. `test_constants.py` reads its own manifest, so no task dependency is needed.
- The backend path filter lists exactly these two manifests, mirrored in the depot shadow. Without it a yaml-only diff never starts the workflow. A wider glob would start CI for manifests that no reader is wired to.
- The obvious fix, a `../feature_flags/mcp/tools.yaml` input, does nothing for selection. Turbo's affected query maps a changed file only to the package that holds it, so the input changes the cache hash and nothing else.
- Blast radius: selection only. An unrelated feature_flags edit still leaves posthog_ai out. posthog_ai is not an isolated product, so selecting it runs the full suite, as any posthog_ai edit already does.

## How did you test this code?

- Ran `turbo query affected --tasks backend:test` against probe commits for a tools.yaml edit, a tools.yaml deletion, an eval_harness edit, and an unrelated feature_flags backend edit. Results match the table above, and the last one selects only feature-flags.
- Ran `turbo-discover.js` end to end on a yaml-only probe diff. It selects posthog-ai and runs the full suite.
- `hogli product:lint` passes for posthog_ai and feature_flags. `hogli lint:workflows` passes.
- Not run: the posthog_ai test suite. This PR changes no test code.

- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

- Came out of triaging the #105034 queue failure through engineering analytics (`broken-tests`, `run-failure-logs`) and `trunk merge status`.
- Skills: `/triaging-merge-queue-failures`, `/writing-tests`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.
- A first version added cross-product input matching with a git diff to `turbo-discover.js`. It was dropped for the native task dependency, which needs no custom diffing and is not tied to the products/ layout.
- CodeRabbit CLI (`--deep`, run on that first version): one finding. A deleted yaml is absent from the dry-run inputs, so the custom matcher missed it. The native approach removed that code, and a deletion probe confirms Turbo handles it.
- Review bots: Codex flagged the wide `products/*/mcp/tools.yaml` glob, and ReviewHog found the tasks reader. Both were fixed. CodeRabbit posted nothing actionable.

## Problem

- Teams already send broadcasts as ordinary workflows: a batch trigger, one email, nothing else. The Broadcasts page lists only workflows created from it, so those sends are invisible there.

## Changes

- The Broadcasts page now also lists ordinary workflows with that shape, tagged "Workflow". Their status and send metrics show like any broadcast.
- A tagged row opens in the workflow editor, not the broadcast wizard, because the wizard would rewrite the workflow's graph.
- The list API gains `broadcast_eligible=true`: broadcasts plus unowned workflows whose trigger action is `batch`, with exactly one `function_email` step and no step other than trigger, email and exit. It is evaluated in Postgres with jsonpath.
- The shape is read from the trigger action, not the legacy `trigger` column, because rows exist where the two disagree.
- The list pages 100 rows at a time with the table's pager, so widening it with workflows never pushes a broadcast out of reach.
- Mechanical: regenerated OpenAPI types and MCP clients.

![Broadcasts list with workflows](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/77ead7f35342ce13a7007dee4f7289186b1f1c83/2026/09/1edc39c3-9c30-4646-acec-e4850eb21e05.png)

## How did you test this code?

Driven in a Playwright browser against the local stack, with this branch's backend applied over the served checkout.

| Step | Observed |
| --- | --- |
| Count the matching rows in Postgres (broadcasts, plus unowned workflows with a batch trigger action, one email and nothing else) | 7 broadcasts, 10 workflows |
| Open `/broadcasts` | 17 rows: 7 broadcasts and 10 tagged "Workflow". Excluded as expected: a batch workflow with a delay, one with no email, and one with two function steps |
| Wait for the row details | Status and metrics settle within 4s (for example, a workflow run shows Sent with 3 sent and 1 opened) |
| Click a tagged row | Opens `/workflows/<id>/workflow` |
| Click a broadcast row | Opens the broadcast summary |
| Add 100 draft broadcasts (removed after) and open the list | "1-100 of 117"; the next page holds the 17 older rows, including the real broadcasts; no row repeats across pages |

`test_list_filter_by_broadcast_eligible` covers the shape rules: two emails, an extra step, an event trigger action under a stale `batch` trigger column, and a loop with the same shape.

## Problem

Five open PRs each add their own copy of `posthog/egress/typesafe/` to call Jev: #101991, #103364, #103555, #104086 and #105577.

- The copies disagree on the budget (60 to 1,000 per minute), the identity (a constant or a key fingerprint), the default lane, and the class names.
- Whichever PR lands first owns the package, and the other four conflict.
- No copy states the rules for sending data to TypeSafe.

## Changes

- One shared TypeSafe egress domain lands first, so each PR rebases onto it and drops its own copy.
- A usage policy at the top of the domain README applies to every caller before merge. The client docstring and the egress `AGENTS.md` point to it:
  - Gate every caller behind a feature flag that reaches PostHog staff only.
  - Send no customer data during the experiment.
  - Before a launch sends customer data, get an explicit per-customer opt-in and sign-off from leadership.
- The budget is one instance-wide key, `typesafe:account:default`, because an instance holds one API key.
- The per-minute default is 600, half of the published 1,200. TypeSafe warns that the limit changes without notice.
- The hourly default is 20,000, an operator ceiling on spend, because TypeSafe bills every input token.
- Callers get the default lane ladder and `NORMAL` by default. No call runs `CRITICAL`, because the state comes from user input.
- The typed `system_one` client covers noul and choice questions. It raises on a partial, out-of-range or wrong-type answer, rather than returning it.
- `TypeSafeRequestFailed.status_code` lets a caller defer a 429 or 529.
- The README cites [docs.typesafe.ai](https://docs.typesafe.ai/models) for every limit, price and header claim.
- Nothing is user-visible. No caller exists on master, and an instance without `TYPESAFE_API_KEY` sends nothing.

## How did you test this code?

- `posthog/egress/test/test_typesafe.py` has four new tests:
  - The request matches the documented body and bearer auth, and the counter records without the key.
  - A 429, 529, non-JSON body, missing answer or out-of-range answer raises instead of returning a partial result.
  - An instance without a key, or a `CRITICAL` call, never calls out.
  - The budget reads the settings it is named after.
- `test_domains.py` passes: the README has its Sources section, and the policy is not flat.
- Not run: repo-wide mypy. A scoped mypy run shows no errors in the new files.

## Problem

The Pi picker and the desktop cloud-task picker disagreed about which models are too old to choose, and the web composer, the Slack App Home picker and the task-defaults settings page applied neither list.

- Opus 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, Sonnet 4.6 and GLM-5.2 were hidden on desktop and offered in the web composer, in Slack, and as a project default.
- Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 were hidden in Pi alone.
- Haiku 4.5 was hidden for cloud tasks and not for Pi, which is the row with no cost chip from [#105098](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/105098).

The two lists named 26 model ids between them, written a week apart and kept in step by nobody.

Second layer of the catalog stack, on [#105701](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/105701). Origin: [Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C0C21VD7GV9/p1790102166474969).

## Changes

- The five pickers now offer the same models. Opus 4.5, 4.6, 4.7, Sonnet 4.6 and GLM-5.2 disappear from the web composer, from Slack and from the task-defaults settings page; Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 come back in Pi.
- A run already on a retired model keeps it. The run starts, the Slack modal no longer clears the stored preference, and the web composer and the settings page still list the model under its own name with its full effort range.
- `CatalogModel` carries `retired`. `isOfferedModel` and `is_offered_model` answer "may a picker offer this", and `HIDDEN_PI_MODEL_IDS`, `BLOCKED_GATEWAY_MODEL_IDS` and `isBlockedModelId` are deleted.

> [!NOTE]
> A model the catalog does not list is no longer offered anywhere. That is what lets 26 ids collapse into one flag on five rows, because most of those ids were gateway models the catalog never named. It also inverts a Pi contract: a model the gateway starts serving now needs a catalog entry before any picker offers it.

Retirement is kept separate from recognition on every surface, which is what protects a pinned run:

| Question | Web | Slack | Desktop |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| May someone pick it? | `pickerModels` | `offered_model_choices` | `isOfferedModel` |
| What is it called, what efforts does it take? | `catalogue` | `available_model_choices` | `catalogModelFor` |

> [!NOTE]
> Two desktop surfaces list a pinned retired model without its catalog name, which this PR does not change. The cloud-task picker renders it through the pre-existing "Custom model" fallback in `buildProviderModelGroups`, because `normalizeGatewayModelsResponse` filters at parse time; the live Pi catalog path has no keep-current branch at all. Both behaved this way for the old deny-listed ids too. Moving that filter out of the parser also changes what `pickAllowedModel` and the Codex `allowed` logic see, so it wants its own PR.

`available_model_choices` in tasks stays permissive on purpose: it answers what a run may use, and the Codex family fallback depends on it accepting an id the catalog does not list.

Mechanical: regenerated projections, catalog snapshot, one mock.

The run path in `agent.ts` asks `catalogModelFor` rather than `isOfferedModel`, so retiring a model never moves a session already pinned to it onto the default.

## How did you test this code?

Automated only, and the desktop app was never launched.

- `isOfferedModel` gets a table of 13 ids it must refuse and 8 it must offer, which is where the deleted lists' coverage went.
- The Pi catalog tests state the new contract: Haiku is dropped, an unlisted model is dropped, Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 are offered.
- `pickerModels` catches the pinned-run regression: dropping a retired model from the recognition list shortens its effort range to the fallback.
- The Slack modal test at `test_initial_options_reflect_current_values` is on Opus 4.7, so it fails if the picker stops listing a stored retired preference. It passes.

Not checked: the local Postgres is unreachable, so every DB-backed test in `test_slack_app_home.py` went unrun, including `TestModalRerender`, which covers the other `_models_for` call. `@posthog/workspace-server` fails 35 tests locally on a `better-sqlite3` ABI mismatch; the file this PR touches there passes on its own.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5 (1M context)

Skills invoked: `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/simplify`.

CodeRabbit CLI pass: skipped. The CLI is signed out, and a signed-out review opens a browser tab, so this opens without a local pass at the author's direction.

No duplicate: `gh pr list --state open --search "model catalog in:title"` found only [#103906](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/103906), which adds Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5 mini to the catalog. If it lands first, both models become offerable and Haiku gets its cost chip, which is compatible with this change and resolves the note above for those two ids.

`/simplify` ran four review agents over the branch and its findings were applied: the web side lost a kea selector in favour of one `pickerModels(catalogue, selected)` call behind `useMemo`, the retirement predicate moved next to `normalizeModelId` in the web catalog half, Slack's rename wrapper went away and its retired-model lookup stopped rebuilding the whole picker tree, and the settings page joined as the fifth surface. Skipped: moving the parse-time filter (see the note above), caching the Slack picker tree (the test fixtures swap catalogue modules per test), and an id-keyed Map for the desktop catalog lookups (every sibling lookup scans the same way).

Two decisions worth recording. Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 stay offered rather than being retired to match Pi, which is the author's call: retiring them would take two current models off the desktop cloud-task picker. And an earlier revision filtered the web composer's `catalogue` itself, which would have clamped a pinned run's effort range to low/medium/high; the split above replaced it.

Follow-ups this leaves: onboarding's free-tier model is `@cf/zai-org/glm-5.2`, which this PR retires, so that constant wants moving to GLM-5.3 Flash.

Public artifact: the diff carries no material from the session.

## Problem

- A reader opening an inbox report that cites a pull request gets a bare `#1234` about half the time, so acting on the report starts with a manual GitHub search.
- Worse across repositories: a bare number reads as the report's own repository, so a cross-repo citation resolves to an unrelated pull request.
- The presentation turn in `report_generation/research.py` styles the summary but says nothing about linking. The shared *Linking what you reference* rule in `scout_harness/prompt.py` does cover linking, but only for PostHog entities, and it never renders into the presentation turn.
- The research turn already runs `gh pr view --json url`, so the URL exists and is then dropped.

Closes #105734

<!-- posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d2b3-f5ac-7957-a70a-7c68459721ae -->
## Origin

- Issues: [#105734](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/issues/105734)
- First signal: 2026-09-24
- Inbox report: [open](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/inbox/reports/01a0d2b3-f5ac-7957-a70a-7c68459721ae)
- Likely cause: [`98cba06`](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/commit/98cba066f3f2719e4ab7acfeb8665ebcf7411a66)
- Task started by: auto-start, after the report was rated P2 and ready to fix
<!-- /posthog-self-driving-origin:01a0d2b3-f5ac-7957-a70a-7c68459721ae -->

## Changes

| | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pipeline presentation turn | no linking rule | renders the pull request rule |
| Scout report channel | PostHog entities only | entities plus pull requests and issues |
| Cross-repo citation | bare number | repository named in the anchor text |
| No URL verified | bare number, silently | bare number, stated as unverified |

- New `products/signals/backend/report_links.py` holds `PULL_REQUEST_LINK_RULE`, the one wording both surfaces render, so the two cannot drift.
- The research protocol now says to keep the `url` each `gh` call returns, because a number alone cannot be turned back into a link later.
- The report title and the summary's first line still stay plain text. The inbox renders both as text, so a link there shows as literal brackets beside a raw URL.
- Mechanical: the constant joins `_RENDERED_IMPORTS`, so a wording change moves `HARNESS_PROMPT_VERSION` and two prompt builds never merge under one id.

## How did you test this code?

- No manual testing. This is prompt text, and its effect only shows in a live research run.
- `products/signals/backend/test/test_research_prompt.py` — added one case asserting the presentation prompt carries the rule and the plain-text carve-out. It catches a regression no existing test did: `build_report_presentation_prompt` composes its sections from a list, and dropping the new one returns every summary to bare numbers with nothing failing.
- `products/signals/backend/test/test_scout_harness.py` — the `_RENDERED_IMPORTS` guard passes, which is what proves the new interpolation is hashed into the prompt version. The database-backed cases in that file error identically on master in this sandbox (no Postgres), so this PR does not change them.
- `hogli lint:tach` and `ruff` pass.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

Updated `products/signals/backend/scout_harness/AGENTS.md`, which describes what `_linking_section` renders. No `docs/` page covers this.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** PostHog Desktop, Claude Opus 5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/editing-agents-md`, `/writing-simplified-technical-english`.
- Duplicate check: `gh pr list --state open --search "signals report summary pull request link"` found nothing covering summary prose. [#104402](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/104402) touches typed report link records, not the prose a summary is written in.
- Considered and rejected: adding a structured pull-request-URL field to the finding artefact. The research and presentation turns share one session, so the agent still holds the URLs it fetched, and a schema change buys nothing the prompt does not already get.
- Also rejected: importing the harness's linking section into `research.py`. `scout_harness` already imports from `report_generation`, so the shared text went into a dependency-light module both sides import instead.
- Public artifact: the diff is prompt text and one test. Nothing in it came from a customer conversation, ticket, or log.
- CodeRabbit CLI was not available in this sandbox, so the PR opens without a local review pass.

---

## Problem

Viewers of recordings with a huge DOM mutation burst see a hole in playback where the frontend excised the burst, with a "playback skips those sections" banner. That excision was a stopgap for a Replayer freeze (a 25k-node style batch blocked the main thread for 92 s). posthog-js 1.434.12 fixes the freeze inside the Replayer by applying batches of 1,000+ adds against a detached subtree, so the frontend no longer needs to drop content. The `replay-oversized-recording-gate` flag that gated the stopgap is fully rolled out and can go.

## Changes

- Recordings with a mutation burst now play in full instead of skipping to the next full snapshot. The oversized-mutations banner and the `recording player skipped oversized mutations` event are gone.
- The 30 MB size gate (`recordingTooLargeToPlay`) stays, now unconditionally. It guards download and memory.
- Mechanical: removed `findOversizedMutationRanges`, the `oversizedMutationRanges` / `hasOversizedMutations` / `playableSnapshotsByWindowId` selectors, and the `REPLAY_OVERSIZED_RECORDING_GATE` constant. The player logic reads `sessionPlayerData.snapshotsByWindowId` again, `featureFlagLogic` is no longer connected in the coordinator.

** will not deploy until posthog-js is bumped to 1.434.12 first

## How did you test this code?

- Removed the burst detection and excision tests, kept the size-gate tests, now without the flag-off rows.
- Ran `sessionRecordingDataCoordinatorLogic.test.ts` and `sessionRecordingPlayerLogic.test.ts` locally, both green.

body:
## Problem

#105251 classifies a failed filter or input by comparing a stamp on the bytecode with the running VM's fingerprint. Nothing writes that stamp yet, so every "this program doesn't fit the runtime" error reads as `legacy`, the owner's problem. That is wrong whenever the runtime is what changed: when #81140 tightened argument counts, `round(19.99, 2)` started throwing in every destination that used it, and without a stamp that files as hundreds of customer mistakes instead of one runtime change.

This PR writes the stamp. It changes nothing about what runs or what is parked.

## Changes

Every piece of bytecode Django compiles now carries `bytecode_contract`, the hash of the runtime it was compiled against, taken from `filter_globals.json`.

- **Filters.** `compile_filters_bytecode` writes `bytecode_contract` next to `bytecode` when the compile succeeds and removes it when it fails. Destinations and hogflow triggers both go through it, so both get stamped.
- **Input templates.** Each hog-templated input gets `bytecode_contract` next to its `bytecode`, for destinations and for function steps in a workflow. Liquid inputs have no bytecode and get no stamp. Transpiled inputs (site apps) drop it.
- **Kept bytecode keeps its own stamp.** When a save can't recompile the filters, the model keeps the last working bytecode. The stamp now travels with it, so old code is never read as freshly compiled.
- **The runtime reads the stamp for inputs too.** The input formatter attaches the failing input's stamp to the error it throws, and the inputs catch block hands it to the classifier. Filters already did this in #105251.
- **A template call the runtime would refuse is refused at save.** `{round(19.99, 2, 3)}` used to compile and then throw on every event. Now the save says so, with the function and the count it takes. Without this the stamp would claim "checked against this runtime" for a call that was never checked, and the runtime would file the failure as a compiler bug instead of a typo.
- **A new stamp alone is not a content change.** Re-saving a destination or a workflow against a newer runtime rewrites every stamp. The revision comparisons for destinations, workflow actions and wait conditions drop the stamp on both sides, so a plain re-save does not create a new version.

Mechanical: `bytecode_contract` joins the derived filter keys that the model and the hogflow API ignore when comparing what a person wrote, the two serializers declare the field so it round-trips, and the Node input schema accepts it.

### What the stamp is, and how it drifts

The stamp is not a hash of the bytecode. It is a hash of the *runtime*: the list of globals, functions and argument counts the Node VM provides at the moment the bytecode is compiled. Read it as "this program was checked against runtime X".

Node generates `filter_globals.json` from its own standard library, and the hash of that file is the runtime's fingerprint. Django reads the same file when it compiles a filter or a template, checks the program against it, and if the program passes, writes the file's hash next to the bytecode as `bytecode_contract`.

Drift is when the program stays the same and the runtime moves. We ship a Node release where the standard library is different: a function removed, an argument count narrowed, a global renamed. The generated file changes with it, so the fingerprint becomes Y. Every destination compiled earlier still carries X. Most runtime changes add things, so most of the time nothing happens. But when a program uses the thing that changed, the VM throws a `contract` error, the classifier sees stamp X on a runtime whose hash is Y, and calls it `drift`: the runtime moved under a program that was valid when we accepted it.

The two other outcomes, for contrast. No stamp at all means the program was compiled before we stamped anything, or could not be recompiled against today's runtime in the backfill, so we cannot know whether the runtime moved: `legacy`. A stamp equal to the current fingerprint with the VM still throwing a `contract` error means the compiler said the program fits this exact runtime and the VM disagrees: `bug`.

One subtlety. The fingerprint changes on any runtime change, including ones that only add a function, so after any deploy every stamp is "older than the runtime". That causes no errors by itself, the class only applies once something throws. It does mean that in the window after a deploy, a real compiler-versus-VM bug reads as `drift` rather than `bug`. Both are ours, both get parked, only the label differs. The backfill re-save moves everything back to the current fingerprint.

### Two examples

**A destination saved today with `{event.uuid}` in its body.** The save compiles the template and writes `bytecode_contract: "bfd6ece60e41383c"` next to it. Nothing else changes. If we later ship a runtime that drops a global this template reads, the runtime's hash moves, the stamp is stale, and the error classifies as `drift`. We see it, we park the events, we replay them after the fix.

**The #81140 case, replayed with stamps in place.** Every destination using `round(x, 2)` has bytecode stamped against the runtime of the day. The deploy changes the declared argument counts, so the runtime's hash changes. Every stamp is now older than the runtime, every error is `contract`, class `drift`. Parked, and replayable once #96261 widens the counts back. The `class="drift"` line on the counter jumping across many teams at once is also the alert.

**Before:** a missing global in a filter or a template always classifies as `legacy`.

**After:** it classifies as `legacy` only when the bytecode has no stamp, as `drift` when the stamp is older than the runtime, and as `bug` when the stamp matches and the VM still refuses it.

> [!NOTE]
> Existing bytecode has no stamp until it is saved again. That is the next PR in this stack, a one-off re-save of the fleet. Until then "no stamp" still means "legacy or never re-saved", and parking stays off.

## How did you test this code?

Tests first, then the code.

- `posthog/cdp/test/test_filters.py`: a successful compile carries the runtime contract, a stale stamp is replaced, a failed compile has none. Catches the stamp going missing or outliving its bytecode.
- `posthog/cdp/test/test_validation.py`: a hog input and a JSON input with templates get the stamp, a liquid input does not. Catches inputs being left out, which is the #81140 path. A template call with too many arguments is refused at save and a correct one is stamped.
- `products/cdp/backend/api/test/test_hog_function.py`: when a save keeps the previous bytecode, it keeps the previous stamp. Catches old code being re-stamped as current. A snapshot that differs only by stamps compares equal, on filters, inputs and mappings.
- `products/workflows/backend/api/test/test_hog_flow_revisions.py`: re-activating a workflow whose stamps changed does not bump its version.
- `products/workflows/backend/api/test/test_hog_flow.py`: a flow's trigger filters carry the stamp.
- `nodejs/src/cdp/utils/invocation-utils.test.ts`: the same missing global on an input classifies as `legacy` without a stamp, `drift` with an older one, and `bug` with the current one.

Ran locally: the filter compiler and validation suites, the destination and workflow API tests named above, the three nodejs suites, mypy on the changed Python modules and the nodejs typecheck. Full backend suite left to CI.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.1

Skills invoked: /writing-tests, /writing-code-comments, /writing-pr-descriptions, /stacking-prs, /reviewing-with-coderabbit.

CodeRabbit CLI: signed out in this session, so the PR opened without a local pass.

Bot review rounds: ReviewHog pushed a commit that keeps stamps out of the workflow revision comparison and flagged the same gap for destination content and for template calls without an arity check, both fixed here. CodeRabbit flagged `fn.filters` being typed nullable in a test, fixed. Greptile flagged the generated API types, regenerated by CI, and asked for workflow function-step input failures to be classified too. After the PR went ready, Greptile and Veria both noted the revision comparison stripped a `bytecode_contract` key anywhere, including inside a person's own JSON body. Valid: it now strips only a stamp that sits beside a `bytecode`, with a test that editing such a key in a webhook body still versions the flow. A missing `-> None` on `visit_call` was added. CodeRabbit noted the transpiled filter path for site apps dropped `bytecode` but would keep a client-sent `bytecode_contract`. Fixed: the field is read-only on the serializer, so only the compiler writes it, and the transpiled path drops it. That is left out on purpose: those failures happen while an action runs, not while an invocation is built, so they never reach the dead-letter path this classification exists for.

Stacked on #105251. The stamp started as a filters-only field in that PR. Tracing the #81140 incident showed the failures were `inputs_failed`, so this PR stamps every compiled bytecode, inputs included, and moves the stamp to where each bytecode lives rather than to a function-level column, because `refresh_hog_functions` recompiles filters without touching inputs and a single stamp would then claim more than it knows.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Problem

- A cloud run that crashes during an ACP call fails with only "Agent server crashed: Internal error", with no cause.
- The run row, the run events, and the sandbox log all lose the real error, so these failures cannot be diagnosed after the fact.
- The ACP SDK is not the cause. When the adapter throws, the SDK answers with `Internal error` and keeps the thrown message in `data.details`.
- `reportFatalError` read only `error.message`, and `Logger.error` kept only `message` and `stack`, so both dropped `data`.

## Changes

The run's error message now carries the adapter's error text:

```diff
 adapter throws Error("<real cause>")
   ACP SDK -> RequestError(-32603, "Internal error", { details: "<real cause>" })
     AgentServer.reportFatalError
-      error_message: "Agent server crashed: Internal error"
+      error_message: "Agent server crashed: Internal error: <real cause>"
```
title: fix(desktop): keep the ACP error details when the agent server crashes

body:
## Problem

A follow-up typed while the agent was working could land in the queue above the composer and stay there. Everything typed afterwards joined it, and nothing reached the agent.

A stop, a finished run, or a failed send holds the staged message on purpose. The hold outlived the message it covered, and a submit into a non-empty queue joins rather than sends.

## Changes

- Submitting lifts a hold left by a stop or a finished run, and the queue goes out at the next turn end.
- A send whose delivery was never confirmed stays held, so an instruction the agent may already have is not repeated.
- Each follow-up keeps its own row, with edit and remove. They still go out as one message.
- A finished run carries the staged rows into the run the next message starts.
- The header counts and collapses the rows, and the send control reads "Send now".

| Waiting on the agent | Held, waiting on you |
| --- | --- |
| ![queued](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/ce822a6d7703e333492c0579c51b50005f179032/2026/09/ad7494d5-9dce-4326-a9a2-6d8cfbb57323.png) | ![held](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/PostHog/pr-assets/e3136fc48ea516eb81adaf554448e158dd69876e/2026/09/e94355f5-e1ce-4aa0-8173-882b43984282.png) |

> [!NOTE]
> A second route to the same symptom is out of scope: a run whose live `_posthog/turn_complete` never arrives leaves the client believing a turn is in flight. That state is produced server-side, and 19.5% of `user_created` runs never persist a turn completion.

## How did you test this code?

- `runInteractionLogic.test.ts` gains a case per fix, including the unconfirmed-delivery path.
- Rendered the `QueuedMessageList` stories at 420px, 520px and 620px, light and dark.
- Not run: the `run-surface` Playwright suite, which needs a running stack.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

None.

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5 (1M context)

A multi-agent QA pass over the branch caught a regression in the first fix: lifting the hold on any submit also lifted it after an unconfirmed delivery. The hold became source-aware as a result, and four dead ends around the queue were fixed alongside it.

Skills invoked: `/writing-tests`, `/writing-ui-components`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/qa-team`.

## Problem

The insight editor saves the insight when a user selects a new chart type. The user does not click Save. A [session recording of the bug](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/replay/01a0cf52-45d5-7a7a-b7d5-d95a108aa417) shows the exact sequence: the user picks a chart type, and the editor exits edit mode and shows an "Insight updated" message within one second. This happens twice in the recording.

## Changes

- `isInsightSceneInstance` (`frontend/src/scenes/insights/insightDataLogic.tsx`) now compares `insightId` and `dashboardId` from `insightSceneLogic` instead of its `insightLogicRef`.
- A listener rebuilds and mounts a new logic instance to set `insightLogicRef`. This work can still be in progress right after the user opens the editor.
- The same action that matches the URL writes `insightId` and `dashboardId`. These values do not lag behind the ref.
- Before this fix, a chart-type click during that gap passed the guard. The editor then sent a PATCH request before the ref caught up.

## How did you test this code?

- Added a regression test to `insightDataLogic.test.ts` that sets a stale `insightLogicRef` while `insightId` and `dashboardId` are already correct. The test fails against the code before this fix, with the same symptom as the bug report. It passes after the fix.
- Ran three test files locally: `insightDataLogic.test.ts`, `insightSceneLogic.test.ts`, and `insightLogic.test.ts`. All 127 tests passed.
- Did not run a manual repro in a browser. No browser was available in this sandbox. Checked the [session recording of the bug](https://us.posthog.com/project/2/replay/01a0cf52-45d5-7a7a-b7d5-d95a108aa417) instead. An AI summary of the recording confirmed two facts: the user did not click Save, and the editor redirected automatically right after the chart-type selection.
- Human note: I tried to repro this in quite a few ways but wasn't able to, it appears to be a race condition that's difficult to trigger, however we can try this fix and see if it continues to occur or not.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Sonnet 5

Investigated a Slack bug report using PostHog session-recording and event data. Found the session that reproduces the bug. Confirmed the click sequence with the replay AI summarizer. Traced the staleness bug in the guard through `insightDataLogic.tsx` and `insightSceneLogic.tsx`.

Skills invoked: `/writing-tests` (extended the existing `persistDisplayOptions` describe block instead of adding a new one; the new test states a concrete regression, and it fails against the code before this fix), `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/writing-simplified-technical-english` (rewrote this description).

No duplicate: searched open PRs for `isInsightSceneInstance`, `insightLogicRef`, "chart type autosave", and `persistDisplayOptions`. No open PR covers this fix.

body:
## Problem

- Someone connecting BigQuery through a Google Cloud service account is blocked at the end of the new-source wizard by an error that lists JSON key fields they never typed.
- The wizard sends the credential fields of both auth options, so the unpicked option's empty key file reaches validation.
- The nested key file config reports each of its own fields as missing.
- Those errors reject the source even when the selected credential is complete.
- A user who picks the key file option and uploads a file that is not a service account key sees the same field list, which names nothing they can fix.

## Changes

- The wizard now names the one action available: upload a key file, or upload a complete one.
- `BigQuerySource.validate_config` drops the key file config's required-field errors before it decides the result, so the unpicked option's empty key file no longer blocks the save. The comment above that check already stated the invariant; the nested validation defeated it.
- A selected key file that is missing fields, or has an empty value in one, gets its own message instead of the field list.
- Mechanical: `missing_field_error` in the shared source config module builds the string both sides match on, so the wording lives in one place.
- A source whose `auth_type` arrives as the bare string naming the option, with the credential fields at the top level, now has its credential checked. It saved with no usable credential before.
- The alternative was to skip the unpicked option inside the shared `validate_config` walker. That changes every source, so the behavior change stays in the BigQuery source.

## How did you test this code?

- Extended the existing parametrized `validate_config` test with three cases, rather than adding a standalone test, because each is a variation of the same behavior.
- Regression caught: a complete service account selection rejected because the form also sent an empty key file. No existing case sent both.
- Regression caught: an uploaded JSON that is not a service account key, which fell through to the raw field list.
- Added one assertion to the shared test body: no returned error names an internal field.
- Added a second parametrized test for the flat payload shape. Regression caught: a bare `auth_type` selection returning early, so a source with no credential validated.
- Added a flat-payload case with an empty `private_key`. Regression caught: a key file whose fields are present but empty validated, because the shared check only tests presence.
- Updated `test_create_external_data_source_missing_required_bigquery_job_input` to the new message. It asserted the old field names.
- Ran the BigQuery source tests and the BigQuery cases in `test_external_data_source.py` locally against Postgres. Not run: the wizard itself.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Fully autonomous

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5

- Skills invoked: `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/writing-user-facing-copy`.
- CodeRabbit CLI pass: the CLI is not installed in this sandbox, so this PR opened without a local pass. The bot review on the PR raised one finding, that a bare `auth_type` selection returns before the credential check. Confirmed against master and fixed, with the regression test above. Copilot returned a quota-limit notice and no findings.
- No duplicate: searched open PRs by source module, by the error wording, and across the maintainer's own open PRs. [#104497](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/104497) is the nearest match. It fixes the frontend so a key file nested in a select option is read at all. It does not change what validation reports once an empty or incomplete key file reaches the backend, and it touches no backend file, so the two do not overlap. With #104497, a file picked and then abandoned for the service account option still reaches the backend as `[{}]`. That payload validates and parses to no key file.
- Follow-up session (Claude Code, Opus 5.5): fixed the failing API test, addressed the CodeRabbit empty-value finding, merged master, and checked the fit with #104497.
- Public artifact: this work started from aggregated source-setup failure counts. No value from that material appears in the diff, the tests, or this description.

---
*Created with [PostHog Desktop](https://posthog.com/desktop?ref=pr)*

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
title: fix(bigquery): stop key file field names blocking source setup

body:
## Problem

- The bump gate in #105731 tests a release against the gateway once, when the pin moves.
- A later Go ai-gateway deploy can break the pinned agent, and no check would catch it before sandbox runs fail.

## Changes

- The 03:00 run of the bump workflow smokes `posthog-sandbox-base:master` on the Go ai-gateway on every night that does not open a bump PR.
- That includes nights when a bump PR is still open or a release was declined, because the pinned agent keeps serving then.
- The run fails as `infra` when `:master` does not hold the pinned agent version.
- A failed run posts in the agent release Slack channel and turns red. An image from before the `agent-smoke` bin reports `unavailable` and stays quiet.

```diff
 03:00 schedule
   resolve pin and npm latest
   if bump   → build PR, image smoke, gateway smoke (#105731), approve
+  else     → gateway smoke on :master (noop, declined, current)
+               not pass → Slack post + red run
```
title: chore(tasks): smoke the pinned sandbox agent nightly on the go ai-gateway

body:
## Problem

- The bump workflow approves a new `@posthog/agent` pin once the image builds and `agent-server --help` starts. Nothing sends a request to a gateway first.
- A release whose default model or request body the Go ai-gateway rejects therefore merges on its own, and every Go-routed sandbox run fails until someone notices.

## Changes

- Before approval, the bump workflow runs one Claude turn and one Codex turn from the bump PR's image through the production US Go ai-gateway, at the release's default models and efforts.
- A failing smoke leaves the PR unapproved. The workflow comments the result table on the PR and the Slack thread says why.

Before:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Bump PR opened]:::phYellow --> B[Image build + agent-server --help]:::phBlue --> C[Approve + /trunk merge]:::phYellow
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
```

After:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Bump PR opened]:::phYellow --> B[Image build + agent-server --help]:::phBlue --> M[Mint agent_smoke token]:::phGray
  M --> S{{"agent-smoke: Claude + Codex"}}:::phBlue --> G[ai-gateway.us.posthog.com]:::phRed
  S -->|both pass| C[Approve + /trunk merge]:::phYellow
  S -->|any other result| W[PR comment, waits for a person]:::phRed
  classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
  classDef phRed fill:#f54e00,stroke:#f54e00,color:#fff;
  classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
  classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
```

- New composite action `sandbox-agent-gateway-smoke`: pull the image, mint one `phe_` token (`product: agent_smoke`, $10 cap, 30-minute TTL), run each runtime, retry a cell once when it comes back `inconclusive`.
- The cap matches the default for real sandbox runs. The gateway reserves the full output limit before each request, and for Opus 5.5 and `gpt-6-sol` that reservation alone can pass $1, which would refuse the first request with a 402. A run spends about $0.32.

| Result | Meaning | Bump |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pass` | Both turns read the nonce with a tool | Approved and enqueued |
| `broken` | The gateway rejected the release (4xx, wrong route, no nonce) | Waits for a person |
| `inconclusive` | 429, 5xx or timeout, twice | Waits for a person |
| `infra` | Pull, mint or credential failed | Waits for a person |
| `unavailable` | The release predates the `agent-smoke` bin | Waits for a person |

- The bump PR body, the approval review, the Slack outcome and `sandboxed-agents.md` now name the gateway smoke. The job timeout grows by the 25-minute step limit.

> [!WARNING]
> Merge this only after both prerequisites exist. Otherwise every bump waits for a person:
> - The org secret `AGENT_SMOKE_AI_GATEWAY_MINT_KEY`: a Go ai-gateway credential that may mint scoped tokens, on a funded internal team. The gateway treats `agent_smoke` as an attribution label, so it needs no gateway code change. A soft daily budget on that product is optional, since each token is capped at $10.
> - An agent release that includes the `agent-smoke` bin from #105730.
title: chore(tasks): smoke the sandbox agent on the go ai-gateway before approval

body:
## Problem

- An agent release can pass the sandbox image smoke and still fail every Go-gateway run: the image smoke only checks that `agent-server --help` starts.
- A release that changes the default model or request shape needs a real turn through the Go ai-gateway to show the break before it reaches sandboxes.

## Changes

- New `agent-smoke` bin in `@posthog/agent`. Each release carries the smoke that matches its own routing code.
- `agent-smoke --runtime claude|codex` drives one turn through `createAcpConnection`, the path `agent-server` uses, on the release's default model and effort.
- Routing comes from `buildGatewayEnv` (#105729). The bin exits `infra` if the env would not route to the Go gateway.
- The turn reads a random nonce from `nonce.txt`. A pass needs `end_turn`, a completed tool call and the nonce in the reply, so the check never grades model prose.
- It prints one JSON line with the token redacted and exits 0 pass, 1 broken, 2 inconclusive, 3 infra.

```text
agent-smoke --runtime codex
  buildGatewayEnv          # AI_GATEWAY_URL + AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN + AI_GATEWAY_PRODUCT(S)=agent_smoke
  runTurn
    createAcpConnection    # same adapter, SDK and binary as agent-server
    initialize → newSession(model = default) → prompt("read nonce.txt")
  classifyFailure          # 429, 5xx, overloaded, timeout → inconclusive; else broken
  → {"runtime":"codex","model":"gpt-6-sol","gateway":"https://ai-gateway.us.posthog.com","result":"pass",...}
```
title: feat(desktop): add an agent-smoke entrypoint that drives one gateway turn

body:
## Problem

- A smoke test for new `@posthog/agent` releases has to route LLM calls exactly as `agent-server` does, or it tests a path production never takes.
- That routing (Go or Python gateway, bearer, attribution headers) sits inside the private `AgentServer.configureEnvironment`, so nothing outside the server can call it.

## Changes

- `buildGatewayEnv` in the new `src/server/gateway-env.ts` holds the routing, unchanged. `configureEnvironment` calls it and keeps its `process.env` writes.
- `codexAuthFromGatewayEnv` moves into the same file.
- Mechanical move. Nothing changes for sandbox runs.

```text
AgentServer.configureEnvironment(input)
  buildGatewayEnv(config, input, logger)   # new, exported
    resolveGatewayTarget                   # Go gateway or Python gateway
    header builders                        # blob or scoped headers
  Object.assign(process.env, POSTHOG_*)    # stays in the server
```
title: chore(desktop): extract the sandbox gateway env into a shared function

body:
## Problem

`cargo install posthog-cli` installs a CLI from last December. crates.io serves **0.5.11**, last updated 2025-12-19, while the CLI is on 0.18.x. The crate has 5,952 downloads and its `repository` field points at this monorepo, so it looks official.

Every other channel is current: npm, Homebrew, the shell installer and the wizard all ship 0.18.5. crates.io is the one that silently does not.

## Changes

- `cargo install posthog-cli` gets the current version. A `publish-cargo` job publishes on every stable release, next to `publish-npm` and `publish-homebrew`.
- Authentication is crates.io Trusted Publishing through `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action`, the same mechanism `publish-symbol-data-crate.yml` already uses. **No `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` secret** to store or rotate; the job exchanges its `id-token` for a short-lived one.
- The job is wired into `notify-released` and `notify-publish-failed`, so a failed publish is reported rather than silent.
- Its gate matches `publish-npm` rather than `publish-homebrew`'s stable-only rule, because crates.io understands prerelease semver and `cargo install` will not pick one by default.

### Where the API bundle comes from

`posthog-cli api` runs `lib/posthog-api-cli.mjs`, which is gitignored and written during the release. Two consequences:

- The job takes it from the release's own `posthog-cli-npm-package.tar.gz` rather than rebuilding from `services/mcp`, so the crate ships the bytes every other channel ships. A rebuild could drift.
- `cli/Cargo.toml` gains an explicit `include`, since cargo packages tracked files and this one is not tracked. Publishing uses `--allow-dirty` for the same reason.

> [!WARNING]
> `build.rs` treats a missing bundle as `None` and still compiles:
>
> ```rust
> } else {
>     "const EMBEDDED_API_CLI_BUNDLE: Option<&[u8]> = None;"
> }
> ```
>
> So a broken extraction would publish a crate whose `posthog-cli api` is dead, and nothing would fail. The job asserts the file is present and non-empty before publishing.

## How did you test this code?

- `hogli lint:workflows` passes all 12 checks across 140 workflows.
- `hogli ci:preflight` passes.
- actionlint reports 5 shellcheck findings on `origin/master`'s copy of this file and 5 on this branch, so the job adds none.
- `cargo metadata` parses the manifest.
- `cargo package --list --allow-dirty` confirms the `include` is complete: **all 63 tracked `src/` files are still packaged**, which matters because an explicit `include` replaces cargo's default and a missing path would break consumers' builds.
- The pinned action SHA `c6f97d4` was resolved from the `v1.0.5` tag and confirmed to be a commit, not a tag object.
- Not run: the publish itself. It only executes during a release, so the first release after this merges is the test.

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None. `cli/RELEASING.md` describes the release flow and channels; a crates.io section belongs there once the first publish is confirmed, rather than describing something untried.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

Written by Claude Opus 5 through Claude Code, driven interactively.

Skills invoked: `/authoring-ci-workflows`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`.

CodeRabbit CLI pass: **not run**. The CLI is installed but signed out, and sign-in opens a browser, so this PR opens without a local pass.

This revives #43789, which added `publish-cli-to-cratesio.yaml` and was closed by the stale bot rather than rejected, with a comment on it asking for Trusted Publishing across all packages. This version differs in two ways: the job lives inside `release-cli.yml` alongside the other channels, so it inherits the release gating and the notification wiring, and it solves the bundle problem the standalone workflow did not address.

A standalone tag-triggered workflow was considered, matching `publish-symbol-data-crate.yml`. It was dropped because a separate workflow would need its own tag trigger, its own version check and its own failure reporting, all of which the release workflow already has.

**Before merging:** Trusted Publishing has to be configured on crates.io for the `posthog-cli` crate, pointing at repository `PostHog/posthog` and workflow `release-cli.yml`. Until then the auth action returns no token and the job fails. The first publish will also jump the crate from 0.5.11 to 0.18.x.

Public artifact: nothing here draws on a customer conversation, ticket or log.
title: feat(cli): publish posthog-cli to crates.io

body:
## Problem

- In the new-session composer, adding a repository takes two clicks on two "Add repositor…" buttons: one opens a dialog, the second opens the picker inside it.
- This was raised in a [Slack thread](https://posthog.slack.com/archives/C09G8Q32R6F/p1790238461608329?thread_ts=1790238461.608329&cid=C09G8Q32R6F).

## Changes

- The repository chip above the prompt now opens an inline multi-select combobox. A pick applies to the task immediately.
- The trigger shows the repository name for one pick, and "N repositories" for more than one.
- The trigger uses the `outline` variant, the same as the "Cloud" select beside it.
- The search field has a gear button that Tab reaches. It opens the old dialog, which keeps the "Use these repositories for the whole space" option.
- Selected repositories stay listed and checked when the remote search page does not include them. Unselected rows disable at the 10-repository limit.

## Problem

An engineer reading a run's trace in the tracing waterfall cannot see the model calls the run made, even when LLM analytics holds them under the same trace id.

- OTel-sourced AI events already carry the app's trace id in `$ai_trace_id`, so the two datasets share a key.
- `ai_events` and `posthog.trace_spans` sit on different ClickHouse clusters, so one HogQL query cannot join them.
- Nothing serves the events half of that join yet. This is the bottom layer of a stack; the layer above draws the rows in the waterfall.

## Changes

- New endpoint `GET /api/projects/:id/tracing/spans/trace/<hex>/ai_events/` returns a trace's `$ai_generation`, `$ai_span` and `$ai_embedding` events, earliest start first.
- An event matches when `$ai_trace_id` is the trace id in either stored form: the 32-hex form OTel ingestion writes, or the hyphenated UUID the LLM gateway writes for a `traceparent` header. The request id is lowercased. Both forms are constants, so the lookup stays on the sort key.
- Each row's `started_at` is normalized across sources. OTel ingestion stamps an event at the span's start, while the SDKs and the gateway stamp it at the finish. The query reads `$ai_ingestion_source`, computes the start, and orders and caps the rows by it, so callers do not have to know which source stamped the event.
- The lookup reads `posthog.ai_events` on its sort key `(team_id, trace_id, timestamp)`. A trace with no AI events costs a primary-key miss, so opening any APM trace stays cheap. There is no time window: the trace id already bounds the read and the table partitions by retention date, so a window prunes nothing.
- It does not use the shared `query_ai_events` resolver on purpose. That resolver probes the `events` table whenever `ai_events` returns nothing, which would scan the team's events on every APM trace without AI calls.
- The action is gated on the `tracing-ai-events` flag, the same flag the frontend layer uses for the waterfall rows, so the endpoint stays dark for anyone the drawer would not show them to.
- The response is LLM analytics data, so the action requires `llm_analytics:read` alongside `tracing:read` and checks the user's viewer access to LLM analytics, the same gate the error-counts action applies for error tracking.
- The requesting user is passed into the HogQL query, so property access rules mask restricted AI columns for that user instead of falling back to the team default.
- Duplicate `ai_events` rows for one event collapse to one row. Each row carries timing, identity, model, tokens, cost and error flag, and no prompt or completion bodies.
- The lookup is capped at 500 rows and does not page. Rows past the `ai_events` retention are not found.
- Mechanical: the facade wrapper, and the regenerated OpenAPI clients for the frontend and the MCP server.

No user-visible change. The endpoint has no caller until the layer above lands, and it answers 403 while the flag is off.

## How did you test this code?

- `products/tracing/backend/tests/test_trace_ai_events.py` guards the case-insensitive match, the event-kind filter, and the response shape. Nothing covered the events side of a trace lookup before.
- A duplicate-row case pins the collapse. Without it a re-delivered event renders twice on the waterfall.
- A parameterized case pins `started_at` for a finish-stamped SDK event, a start-stamped OTel event, and an SDK event with no latency. Without the last one a missing latency yields a null start.
- A case pins the match on the gateway's UUID form. Without it gateway calls silently never appear.
- Two cases pin that a junk `$ai_latency` (1e20, negative) is returned as null instead of failing the lookup.
- A case pins the 400 on a non-hex id.
- A parameterized case pins the 403 for a member whose LLM analytics access is `none`, and the 200 for a viewer. Without it a tracing-only member reads model and cost data.
- A case pins the 403 with the flag off.
- Not verified: the query against production data.

- [x] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Claude Fable 5.1

Skills: `/improving-drf-endpoints`, `/stacking-prs`, `/writing-tests`, `/writing-code-comments`, `/reviewing-with-coderabbit`, `/writing-pr-descriptions`.

CodeRabbit CLI: ran with `--deep` against master on the first revision. No findings. Not re-run after the query moved from `events` to `ai_events`.

Review threads: the missing `llm_analytics` scope and access check, and the missing user on the HogQL query, were both valid and are fixed. The gateway UUID form and the OTel start-stamp semantics were both valid and are fixed. The stored-id case finding is rejected: OTel ingestion hex-encodes ids lowercase, and a case-insensitive match on `ai_events.trace_id` would lose the sort key the table switch exists for. The docstrings no longer claim a case-insensitive match on the stored side.

Decisions: the first revision queried the shared `events` table inside a two-hour window and also matched the cloud runner's `task_run_trace_id` property. That read every AI event of the team in the window on every drawer open, so it moved to `ai_events` on the sort key, and the custom property match went with it (it is not a column). The cloud runner's events therefore do not join until the run's trace id reaches `$ai_trace_id`. Duplicate search (`gh pr list --search "ai events trace"`) found nothing.

body:
## Problem

- A developer can add `` api.get(`api/projects/${id}/…`) `` anywhere in `frontend/src`, and CI passes. More than 400 of these calls exist today.
- Each raw call hand-writes the URL and the response type. A backend change breaks it at runtime, not at compile time.
- `prefer-codegen-api` blocks raw calls only under `products/*/frontend/`. The `lib/api.ts` ratchet cannot see them, because the URL never passes through `lib/api.ts`.
- This PR is the base of a stack. Later layers migrate the calls and add missing OpenAPI schemas.

## Changes

- A new raw `api.<verb>(...)` call anywhere in the frontend now fails CI at ERROR. Outside the API layer, code calls the generated functions.
- The API layer stays exempt: `lib/api.ts`, `api-orval-mutator.ts`, `api-stream.ts`, generated code, and test and spec files, which exercise the transport on purpose.
- The rule now also catches `getResponse`, `createResponse`, `createWithUploadProgress`, `stream` and `loadPaginatedResults`, which all take a URL.
- A suppression now needs a reason: `prefer-codegen-api-reason` fails a bare `// nosemgrep: prefer-codegen-api` with nothing after ` -- `.
- Every existing call gets a `// nosemgrep: prefer-codegen-api -- Legacy raw API call …` line, 536 in 205 files:

| Marker says | Sites | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `Use <fn>() from '<module>' instead.` | 186 | A generated function serves the same route and method, and its types describe the call |
| `<fn>() … serves this route, but its generated types do not describe this call yet …` | 97 | The function exists, but it returns `void` or its parent's type, or takes no body for a call that sends one, so the endpoint schema needs fixing first |
| `No generated function covers this endpoint yet …` | 178 | The generated client skips the endpoint: no schema, no product tag, or excluded from the spec |
| `… URL built at runtime …` | 71 | Helper-built or server-returned URL |
| `… route outside /api/ …` | 4 | Non-API Django route |

- Markers, not a baseline file: the security semgrep job is diff-aware on pull requests but scans everything on master pushes. Unmarked debt would turn master red. Markers also survive file moves.
- The 107 bare `// nosemgrep: prefer-codegen-api` lines in `products/` get the same wording, so `git grep -c "Legacy raw API call"` counts all remaining debt.
- Everything outside the rule file and its fixture is mechanical: one comment line per call site. One marker sits at the end of its call line, because oxfmt moves it onto a ternary otherwise.

> [!NOTE]
> An open PR that adds a raw call in `frontend/src` fails semgrep once this lands. The fix is the generated function, or a marker with a reason for a URL the server returns. The comment-density check flags this PR because every added line is a marker.

## How did you test this code?

- New fixture cases in `prefer-codegen-api.test.ts` for the five added verbs, plus a bare and a reasoned suppression for the reason rule. Each fails if its pattern regresses.
- Scanned `frontend/src` and `products` with the widened rule: zero findings with local semgrep 1.177 and with the CI image 1.167.0. A plain regex scan found no call that semgrep missed.
- `oxfmt --check` on every touched file.
- Checked a sample of the suggested functions against their route and method. A marker only says "Use" when the function's response type is neither `void` nor its parent resource's type, and a write that sends data maps to a function with a body.
- Not checked: request bodies. A function whose response type looks right can still take the wrong request body, so the migration layers verify types per call.
- Not run: the TypeScript check, because the diff only adds comment lines.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?
