## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (`claude-opus-5-5`)

- Direction from the assignee: an ERROR rule for raw calls everywhere, a loud marker at each existing site as the base, then migration and schema layers.
- A one-off script placed the markers. It took semgrep's JSON output for locations, and matched each route and HTTP method against the URL getters in every generated `api.ts`. The match also follows the documented twin of a hidden route: flat `projects/{id}/…` actions are generated under `organizations/{id}/projects/{id}/…`, and the legacy root `cohort/` and `person/` paths under `projects/{id}/…`. The script is not committed.

body:
## Problem

- Split product shards plan from one master run's timings, so one run's noise decides how balanced they are.
- Core and Temporal already plan from an average of the last five runs ([#65983](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/65983)). Products never got it.
- Product timings live in the products slice of the union `.test_durations`, and [#104858](https://github.com/PostHog/posthog/pull/104858) now splits product shards by file from that slice.
- Needs the layer below: without it, every older run fails the Products drift check and the average holds only the newest run.

## Changes

- The hourly timing refresh averages the products slice over the same runs as the Core and Temporal plans.
- Each older run goes through the same Products path as the newest one, drift check included. A run that fails it stays out of the average.
- The newest slice goes first, so it decides which tests the average keeps. After a drift fallback the previous slice stays as it is, with no averaging.
- The newest run's product artifacts are already downloaded, so they are not fetched twice.
- The job timeout goes from 10 to 15 minutes for the four extra runs' product artifacts, the largest artifact set.
- Product shards keep reading the union. There is no new file, no new pytest-split flag, and no product job change.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph Before
        A1[Newest master run] --> B1[Products slice]
        B1 --> C1[(Union .test_durations)]
    end
    subgraph After
        A2[Newest master run] --> B2[Products slice]
        O2[Four older runs] --> P2[Products slices that pass the drift check]
        B2 --> M2[Average]
        P2 --> M2
        M2 --> C2[(Union .test_durations)]
    end
    classDef phYellow fill:#f9bd2b,stroke:#f9bd2b,color:#000;
    classDef phBlue fill:#1d4aff,stroke:#1d4aff,color:#fff;
    classDef phGray fill:#e5e7eb,stroke:#c7ccd1,color:#000;
    class A1,A2,O2 phYellow;
    class B1,B2,P2,M2 phBlue;
    class C1,C2 phGray;
```

## How did you test this code?

- Replayed the products part of the refresh on the real artifacts of five recent master runs, with the layer below applied.
  - All five slices passed the drift check. The average kept the same 116k tests and the JUnit scale marker.
  - Per-product totals moved by a few percent, so shard counts stay about the same.
  - Processing the four extra runs took about 30 s locally.
- Replayed split plans on product JUnit from seven recent master runs, scored on a newer run the plan did not see:

| Plan source | Slowest shard over the mean, average of 16 cases | Worst case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One run (today) | 6.4% | 16.2% |
| Five-run average | 4.2% | 12.5% |

- The biggest single gains: warehouse-sources 14.5% to 5.3%, product_analytics 14.4% to 7.1%.
- `hogli lint:workflows` passes.
- Not checked: a live refresh on master. The first hourly refresh after merge shows the extra download time and the `Averaged ... across N run(s)` line for Products.

## Release status

- [x] No feature flag controls this change <!-- release-status: no-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change is behind a feature flag and is not available to users <!-- release-status: behind-feature-flag -->
- [ ] This change makes a previously flagged feature available to everyone <!-- release-status: fully-available -->

## Automatic notifications

- [ ] Publish to changelog?

## Docs update

None.

## 🤖 Agent context

**Autonomy:** Human-driven (agent-assisted)

**Agent:** Claude Code, Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5)

- The first idea was a separate `.test_durations.products` plan file passed through `--split-plan-path`. It was dropped: a plan file skips path scoping in the plugin, and one shared file would make each product plan against every product's tests. Averaging inside the union needs no new file and no plugin change.
- An earlier assessment rejected multi-run product averaging for sizing, where run-to-run variation of product totals is small. The replay above measures splitting balance instead, where per-test noise matters.

## Problem

Terminal users can stall when listing a folder because filename detection paginates every notebook and SQL insight in the project.
Folder links ignore their query parameter, and Doom ignores the configured WASD controls.

## Changes

- Directory listings use only the filesystem API, with page-scoped content types checked against backing-object permissions. File contents load on open.
- Folder URLs honor `?folder=...`, including navigation without a remount.
- Terminal folder links reveal the folder in the Files tab when `simple-sidepanel` is enabled, including folders loaded asynchronously.
- Links to another project retain their project destination. Other users open the Files page.
- Doom supports W/S movement, A/D strafing, arrow turning, Space firing, E use, and mouse turning through **Capture mouse**.
- Optional tools appear in this order: node, pi, nyancat, doom.
- Generated API types are mechanical updates for the opt-in content-type parameter.

The binary fix merged in [terminal-assets #2](https://github.com/PostHog/terminal-assets/pull/2). This PR pins the merged, checksum-verified build.
